dimension: Independent critical review of the EvidenceDS v0.1 draft (spec, gate.py, contracts, tests) and a re-check of the ai-data-science-team claims, judged against a 6-12 month enterprise delivery budget

findings.claim: KEEP: The draft tracks three separate statuses: execution_status, check_outcome and promotion. Missing, ERROR and INCONCLUSIVE results become HOLD and never PASS. These are the right core ideas, and they prevent exactly the 'failure reported as success' bug seen in ai-data-science-team.
findings.evidence: Spec defines SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELLED vs PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE/ERROR vs ALLOW/HOLD/REJECT. It forbids voting, averaging, or treating an exhausted budget as 'done'. gate.py turns missing evidence into HOLD. By contrast, ADST issue #90 returns 'Workflow completed.' after a wrangler failure.

findings.claim: KEEP: The leakage and label-maturity rules are the most reusable IP in the draft. They should be packaged as a check library and agent skills, not as a platform.
findings.evidence: The rules include an available_at <= cutoff check, 'immature label unknown_not_negative', per-fold fit, OOF target encoding, and declared join cardinality (m:1 must not add rows). The holdout is isolated by account/mount/credential, not by directory. The scorer never loads candidate pickles. The 24-item fault-injection list is a good seed for an eval suite.

findings.claim: KEEP: The business-value discipline is sound. G5 (bounded experiment) is kept separate from G6 (scale-up/value claim), Shadow is not counted as value evidence, ITT and SRM checks are required, and 'value_proven: false' is the default.
findings.evidence: The spec says G6 must not be a prerequisite for starting an experiment. Shadow validates only plumbing and latency. Explicit non-goals and an honest statement of limits are included.

findings.claim: ai-data-science-team: the 'silent failure' and 'routing' claims are CONFIRMED by recent open issues that have no maintainer response.
findings.evidence: #90 (2026-10-14): after the initial attempt plus 3 fix retries, the wrangler error is dropped and the result shown is 'Workflow completed.' or a chart built from raw data. #89: generated code drops duplicates, so totals are off by 0.4-8.4%. #85: invented answers. #87: the routing refusal is ignored. #88: text appended to a question is executed as part of the task. #70 (exec injection) has been open since 2026-01-09.

findings.claim: ai-data-science-team: the 'no sandbox' claim is OUTDATED or imprecise. A subprocess sandbox at the Python level now exists for 4 agents. The template exec paths, including the SQL path with a live DB connection, still run raw in-process exec().
findings.evidence: utils/sandbox.py (335 lines) uses an import blocklist (os, sys, subprocess, socket ...), restricted builtins, a socket monkeypatch, RLIMIT_AS of 512 MB and a 10 s timeout. It is called by the cleaning, wrangling, visualization and feature-engineering agents. agent_templates.py still has exec(agent_code, global_vars, local_vars) at ~L591 and ~L685. The sandbox injects pd/np and allows getattr/type/object. That leaves pandas file I/O and introspection escapes open, so this is not OS isolation.

findings.claim: ai-data-science-team: the 'no tests' claim is CONFIRMED, and the project is effectively in maintenance limbo. Use it only as a UX reference, not as a foundation.
findings.evidence: The recursive tree of master (151 paths) contains no test files. The last push was 2026-01-28 ('new supervisor example - not yet working', then 'works'). It has 5,463 stars, 38 open issues+PRs, MIT license, and its README says 'Beta... breaking changes until 0.1.0'.

findings.claim: BUG in gate.py: unauthenticated evidence can force REJECT. This contradicts its own trust model ('Evidence may arrive from untrusted transport; it is authenticated here').
findings.evidence: Grouping, unexpected-check and ambiguity rules (L152-167) run BEFORE HMAC verification (L172-179). A local probe confirmed it: adding an unsigned record with the same check_id turned ALLOW into REJECT ('q:ambiguous_multiple_records'), and an unsigned record with an unknown check_id also gave REJECT. Since REJECT is the terminal 'candidate is bad' verdict, anyone who can post evidence can veto any candidate. Fix: authenticate and filter first, and turn unverifiable input into HOLD plus a security alert.

findings.claim: BUG/contradiction: gate.py has no supersede or retry semantics. Normal operations produce REJECT, against the spec's own retry and revocation design.
findings.evidence: Probe: a signed ERROR followed by a retried signed PASS for the same subject gives REJECT, and two honest PASS records also give REJECT. Yet the spec says to retry transient failures (L407) and EvidenceRecord has supersedes/revokes (L145), which gate.py ignores. Key rotation produces unknown_signer_key, which is REJECT rather than HOLD (L172-175).

findings.claim: The test suite overstates what it verifies.
findings.evidence: test_conflicting_votes_cannot_override_failure (L69-72) passes because of the ambiguous_multiple_records rule, not because FAIL dominates; two PASS records also REJECT. The 6 tests in test_domain_properties.py test helper functions defined inside the test file (L6-22), not product code. Hypothesis is named in the core stack (spec L11, R24) but is not used. In practice, '39 passed' means about 33 tests of a single 98-line function.

findings.claim: OVER-ENGINEERED: the custom Evidence Ledger, HMAC signing, 17-table PG schema, 13-endpoint API and reconciler duplicate commodity tooling. Signed, identity-bound evidence and gated promotion are available off the shelf.
findings.evidence: actions/attest signs in-toto statements (subject digest + custom predicate) with Sigstore short-lived certs. Private repos require GHE Cloud. GitHub environments offer up to 6 required reviewers, a prevent-self-review option, and secrets withheld until approval. GitLab protected environments and deployment approvals require Premium. Dagster asset checks support blocking=True. Databricks MLflow 3 deployment jobs (Public Preview) run evaluate, approve, then deploy. The spec itself says 'do not invent crypto protocols' (L286).

findings.claim: CONTRADICTION: separation of duties is cosmetic at the stated team size. Real separation should come from CI service identities, not app-level keys held by people.
findings.evidence: L20 requires distinct identities for the code worker, evaluator and release controller, but L501 lets one person hold every role. With symmetric HMAC, the gate must hold every producer key (gate.py L172-177), so whoever runs the gate can forge any evidence. CI OIDC identities plus protected environments give separation without key management.

findings.claim: OVER-ENGINEERED and wrongly sequenced: about 14 named components and 8 PRs, with the Agent Adapter last (PR8). The 'agentic' value lands after the budget is likely spent, and mandating Dagster clashes with enterprises' existing orchestrators.
findings.evidence: Dagster self-hosting needs a webserver, a daemon and user-code services (L419), on top of the MLflow server, PG with 3 DBs, the FastAPI API, a Podman runner and the release reconciler. L49 makes Dagster the 'only lifecycle scheduler', yet L93 and L97 say to reuse what already exists, e.g. dbt and the data-versioning system. Chinese enterprises commonly run DolphinScheduler, Airflow or DataWorks.

findings.claim: MISSING: there is no semantic layer or governed metric definitions as the ground truth of meaning. The industry standardized on one in 2026.
findings.evidence: Grep finds no semantic-layer, metric-registry or catalog content. The TaskSpec primary_outcome is a free string. OSI v1 was released 2026-01-27 under Apache-2 and covers datasets, metrics, dimensions, relationships and contexts. Members include Snowflake, Salesforce, dbt Labs, Databricks, Cube and ThoughtSpot. dbt executes definitions through MetricFlow.

findings.claim: MISSING: context engineering for agents (catalog, verified queries, skills). Vendors, including Chinese ones, now ship exactly this.
findings.evidence: Snowflake has a Verified Query Repository (question + verified SQL). Databricks Genie has trusted assets and example SQL. Alibaba DataWorks' new Data Agent is built on Qwen Code with official Skills, custom SKILL.md (<=200 KB) or zip (<=50 MB) uploads, and model options qwen3.7-max (default), qwen3.8-max, deepseek-v4-pro and glm-5.2. Agent Skills is an open format, at agentskills.io. The draft's 'context minimization' (L305) covers only redaction, not supplying meaning.

findings.claim: MISSING: analytics Q&A (NL to SQL / ChatBI), most likely the highest-volume DS/analytics workload, has no design at all. Only the ML path is engineered.
findings.evidence: 'Analytical task' is listed as a legal endpoint (L30), but there is no flow, eval or interface for it, and grep finds no text-to-SQL, ChatBI or 问数 content. Vendors' flagship data agents center on it: Genie, Cortex Analyst and DataWorks ChatBI. No quantitative survey of request mix was verified.

findings.claim: MISSING: data engineering beyond ingestion: dbt/SQL change, pipeline break-fix, backfill, SLA and alerting. This is where agents still fail most and where hours saved are measurable.
findings.evidence: dbt appears only as 'connect existing dbt tests' (L93), and grep finds no backfill, SLA or alerting content. On the Spider 2.0 leaderboard, Spider2-DBT (68 repo-level tasks, added 2025-05-22) tops out at 65.6, versus 96.70 on Spider2-Snow and 76.23 on Spider2-Lite. Entries are self-submitted and undated. The dbt MCP server already exposes lineage, model health and test-detail tools.

findings.claim: MISSING: eval-set design for the agents themselves. The draft's holdout discipline should also cover agent context.
findings.evidence: Snowflake: a verified query 'can either guide Cortex Analyst at runtime or be used as evaluation ground truth, but not both'; evals run on a temporary copy without those queries and track regressions. Genie: up to 500 benchmark questions, result-set match, 2-4 phrasings each, and benchmarks are never used as context. The draft's A/B/C/D comparison (L495) has no golden question set or grading rule.

findings.claim: MISSING: an LLM data-residency and model-routing policy. The draft says only 'external strong models allowed, redacted summaries only'.
findings.evidence: China, cross-border provisions (2024-03-22): non-CIIO exporting <100k persons/yr of non-sensitive PI is exempt; 100k-1M persons or <10k sensitive requires a standard contract or certification; important data is excluded. AIGC labeling measures apply from 2025-09-01. Public-facing GenAI services need filing: 748 filed by 2025-12-31 (reported). EU: Annex III high-risk obligations were provisionally deferred to 2027-12-02 on 2026-05-07, pending formal adoption.

findings.claim: OUTDATED: the agent integration surface. The spec treats MCP as an afterthought adapter over a custom FastAPI. MCP is now vendor-neutral and stateless, with enterprise auth and a long-running-task extension.
findings.evidence: MCP was donated to the Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation) on 2025-12-09. Spec 2026-07-28 removes the initialize handshake, deprecates DCR in favor of CIMD, and moves Tasks into the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension, which fits /v1/runs polling. The page also names an Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension. The draft also lacks on-behalf-of identity propagation and row-level security for agent queries.

findings.claim: MISSING: agent observability and online evaluation, even though MLflow (already chosen) provides them in open source.
findings.evidence: The draft uses MLflow only for classic ML. MLflow 3.x OSS has tracing, GenAI evaluation datasets, make_judge (3.4), multi-turn eval (3.7), online-monitoring judges on traces and distributed tracing (3.9), plus OTel metrics export. Grep finds no tracing or observability content for agents in the spec.

findings.claim: MISSING: a cost/ROI model with kill criteria. This is the main reason agentic projects get cancelled.
findings.evidence: The spec has no token, ROI or cost-per-use-case model. L493 lists 'total cost per correct task' with no baseline or target. Gartner (June 2025) predicts that >40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by end-2027 because of cost, unclear value or risk controls. MIT NANDA (2025, preliminary: 52 interviews, 153 surveys) reports only ~5% of custom enterprise AI reaching production.

findings.claim: MISSING: adoption and change management: workflow embedding, training, a feedback-to-context loop, and owners for metric and verified-query curation.
findings.evidence: Grep finds no training, adoption or change-management content. Human roles (L499) are limited to approval. MIT NANDA attributes failures to a 'learning gap' and poor fit with workflows, with systems not retaining feedback. The vendor pattern turns usage into curated verified queries (Snowflake suggests VQRs from usage).

findings.claim: DESIGN FLAW in the first vertical: a churn-risk classifier ranking customers for retention contact is the textbook case where risk-based targeting underperforms. The baseline and metric are also inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Ascarza, 'Retention Futility', JMR 55(1), Feb 2018: targeting by lift beats targeting by risk. That violates the draft's own principle that prediction is not intervention evidence (L32). The task.yaml baseline is 'existing_policy', yet the primary metric is Brier non-inferiority (L54, L62-64), which is undefined if the current policy emits no probabilities.

findings.claim: RISK: 'raw data local-first' snapshots into DuckDB/Parquet conflict with how enterprise data is governed and create ungoverned shadow copies.
findings.evidence: L9 says '原始数据本地优先' (raw data local-first) and L185 says snapshots go into an isolation area. Enterprise data sits in warehouses with RBAC, row-level security and masking (MaxCompute/Hologres/StarRocks/Snowflake/Databricks). Agents should push queries down to the warehouse under the user's identity, with DuckDB used for samples, dev and CI fixtures.

corrections_to_common_beliefs: 'ai-data-science-team has no sandbox' is imprecise. Since 2026 it has utils/sandbox.py (a subprocess with an import blocklist, restricted builtins, a socket shim, a 512 MB RLIMIT_AS and a 10 s timeout) for 4 agents. It is a bypassable Python-level sandbox, and agent_templates.py still runs raw exec(), including the SQL path with a live connection.

'Fail-closed' in gate.py is not the same as safe. Rejecting on unauthenticated or duplicate input turns transport noise, retries or key rotation into a terminal REJECT. Unverifiable input should produce HOLD plus an alert, and REJECT should require an authenticated FAIL.
'39 tests passed' does not show the core works. Roughly 33 tests cover one function, 6 test helpers defined inside the test file, and the 'conflicting votes' test passes for an unrelated reason.

Trustworthy gating does not need a custom HMAC evidence ledger. CI OIDC identity plus Sigstore/in-toto attestations (actions/attest) and protected environments with required reviewers and no self-approval provide signed, identity-bound evidence and promotion control off the shelf.

MCP is no longer one vendor's protocol or a thin afterthought. It is governed by the AAIF (Linux Foundation) since 2025-12-09, and spec 2026-07-28 has a stateless core, deprecates DCR in favor of CIMD, and moves Tasks into an extension. It should be the primary agent interface, backed by the same authz service.

'Enterprise text-to-SQL is ~20% accurate' is stale. That 21.3% figure is from the 2024 Spider 2.0 paper. Current self-reported leaderboards show Spider2-Snow at 96.70 and Spider2-Lite at 76.23, but repo-level dbt tasks (Spider2-DBT) at 65.6 and DABstep-hard at 14.55% at launch. Multi-step data engineering and analysis, not single SQL generation, is the hard frontier, and leaderboard numbers are not your data.
Dagster asset checks do not block downstream assets by default; they need blocking=True. The draft is correct on this (L70).
EU AI Act Annex III high-risk obligations are no longer expected on 2026-08-02. A provisional deal (2026-05-07) moves them to 2027-12-02, and Annex I to 2028-08-02, pending formal adoption.
design_implications: Re-scope v1 around high-volume, measurable workflows: (a) governed analytics Q&A over a semantic layer with verified queries; (b) data-engineering change and break-fix agents (dbt/SQL PRs, failed-job triage, backfills) gated by CI. Make the ML lifecycle (the churn/tabular path) a later task pack. Agents ship in month 1-3, not in PR8.

Buy or reuse: the warehouse and its semantic layer (dbt MetricFlow / OSI-compatible, Cube, or Snowflake semantic views / DataWorks), the existing orchestrator (Airflow, DolphinScheduler or DataWorks rather than a mandatory new Dagster), GitHub/GitLab CI with protected environments, and MLflow for both the model registry and agent tracing/evals. Build only: the check library, a gate policy step, an MCP server plus skills, an eval harness, and the ROI dashboard.

Keep gate.py's semantics but run it as a policy step inside the CI deploy job. Store evidence as in-toto statements signed with the CI OIDC identity next to the artifacts. Drop the custom HMAC, the 17-table ledger DB and the reconciler from v1. Fix three things: authenticate before counting, add supersede/retry semantics, and HOLD on unverifiable input.

Treat metric definitions as versioned ground truth. Add metric_definition_digest and semantic_model_digest to the evidence subject, so a metric-definition change invalidates downstream answers and models just as a data change does.

Make MCP the primary agent surface. Tools: catalog/metric lookup, verified-query execution, check runs, PR proposals and run status via the Tasks extension. Package procedures as Agent Skills (SKILL.md) and propagate end-user identity (on-behalf-of plus row-level security). Execute generated code only in OCI/gVisor containers per the draft's deployment profile, never through Python blocklists as ADST does.

Design the evals first. Build golden question and task sets from real query logs and tickets, grade by result-set equality with 2-4 paraphrases, and keep benchmark items out of the runtime context (the Snowflake/Genie rule, the same as the draft's holdout principle). Track regressions on every model, prompt or skill change, and report cost per correct answer.

Add a model-routing matrix by data class and jurisdiction. Default to metadata- or schema-only prompts. For PI or important data in China, use domestic models (Qwen/DeepSeek/GLM, self-hosted or on in-region cloud). Use regional endpoints elsewhere. Log every prompt and context artifact for audit. Check filing and labeling duties if anything is public-facing.

Write an ROI plan before building. Record baseline hours per request type, the current backlog/SLA, target deflection, LLM plus infra cost per correct task, and kill/continue criteria at months 3 and 6. Embed the agent where users already work (BI, DingTalk/Feishu/WeCom, IDE), name owners for metric and verified-query curation, and turn user feedback into verified queries.
Do not fork or build on ai-data-science-team. Its silent-failure, routing and exec issues are open with no maintainer activity since 2026-01. At most, borrow UX ideas from its AI Pipeline Studio.

If the retention case stays, design it as uplift or experiment-first: use randomized historical contacts or start with a G5 experiment. Pick a baseline metric that the existing policy can actually be scored on.
open_questions: What does the target enterprise already run (warehouse, orchestrator, BI, git hosting tier)? This decides buy vs build. For example, GitLab deployment approvals need Premium, and GitHub artifact attestations for private repos need GHE Cloud.
What is the actual request mix (ad-hoc Q&A vs pipeline break-fix vs ML projects) and the baseline hours per type? Measure it from ticket and query logs; no verified public statistic was found.
Which data classes and jurisdictions apply (China PI or important data, EU)? Is any output public-facing, which would trigger GenAI filing and labeling?
Is OSI actually importable or exportable in the chosen tools today? dbt describes OSI support as a plan.
Spider 2.0 leaderboard entries are self-submitted and undated. Verify the agent vendors' claims on in-house golden sets before choosing a model or agent.
Team size and budget: is 2-4 engineers realistic for even PR1-PR6 in 6-12 months, and which PRs can be replaced by CI and platform features?

dimension: Regulatory, legal and social constraints on AI agents doing data science on enterprise data (EU / China / US / other), status as of 2026-10-19

findings.claim: The EU AI Act 'Digital Omnibus on AI' is now law as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Stand-alone Annex III high-risk obligations moved from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027. High-risk AI embedded in Annex I products moved to 2 Aug 2028.
findings.evidence: The Commission proposed it on 19 Nov 2025 and a provisional deal followed on 7 May 2026. Parliament voted on 16 Jun 2026 and the Council adopted it on about 29-30 Jun 2026. It was published in the OJ on 24 Jul 2026 and entered into force on 27 Jul 2026. Annex III covers employment, education and credit assessment, among others.

findings.claim: Other changes in the Omnibus: (1) Article 50 transparency duties (disclosing AI interaction, deepfake and AI-content marking) were not delayed and apply from 2 Aug 2026. GenAI systems already on the market get until 2 Dec 2026 for machine-readable marking. (2) New bans on nudifier and CSAM-generation systems apply from 2 Dec 2026. (3) The AI-literacy duty (Art. 4) is softened to 'taking measures to support' staff literacy. (4) Deployers, and providers of non-high-risk systems, may now process special-category data to detect bias, only exceptionally and with safeguards. (5) Registration in the EU database is reinstated with lighter content. (6) Some SME exemptions now also cover small mid-caps. (7) The AI Office gets exclusive supervision of some AI systems built on GPAI models.
findings.evidence: Addleshaw Goddard: Article 50 applies from 2 Aug 2026, with a grace period to 2 Dec 2026 for systems placed on the market earlier. NatLawReview: the AI Office can impose periodic penalty payments of up to 5% of average daily turnover.

findings.claim: GPAI-model obligations (Chapter V) have applied since 2 Aug 2025. The AI Office's enforcement powers over GPAI providers took effect on 2 Aug 2026: requesting documentation, running evaluations, ordering mitigation or withdrawal, and fines of up to 3% of turnover or €15M. Models placed on the market before 2 Aug 2025 have until 2 Aug 2027. The GPAI Code of Practice is voluntary but is used as a de facto conformity benchmark; Meta and the major Chinese labs reportedly did not sign.
findings.evidence: Art. 101 fine ceiling: 3% of worldwide turnover or EUR 15M. The Omnibus did not delay any GPAI obligations.

findings.claim: The Commission's guidelines on high-risk classification under Article 6 (statutory deadline 2 Feb 2026) exist only as a draft, published on 19 May 2026 with examples of systems that are and are not high-risk. The final version was not out as of the latest sources (expected around end-2026).
findings.evidence: IAPP: the draft was delivered 'after delays'. Reports disagree on whether the consultation closed on 23 Jun or 23 Jul 2026.

findings.claim: Under EU AI Act Art. 26, deployers of high-risk systems, which now applies from Dec 2027 for Annex III, must: assign human oversight to people with the necessary competence, training and authority; keep automatically generated logs for at least 6 months; inform workers' representatives and affected workers before using such a system at work; and use the provider's information to carry out a GDPR Art. 35 DPIA.
findings.evidence: Art. 26(6) text: logs are kept 'of at least six months, unless provided otherwise' by law.

findings.claim: GDPR interplay: in C-203/22 Dun & Bradstreet Austria (27 Feb 2025), the CJEU held that people subject to automated credit scoring are entitled to a meaningful explanation of the procedure and principles actually applied. Simply handing over the algorithm is not enough. A counterfactual explanation (how different inputs would change the result) may be appropriate. Trade secrets must be disclosed to the DPA or court for balancing rather than withheld outright.
findings.evidence: The Court said communicating the algorithm is not 'a sufficiently concise and intelligible explanation'. This builds on SCHUFA (C-634/21, 2023), which treated scoring itself as an Art. 22 decision.

findings.claim: The GDPR part of the Digital Omnibus (COM(2025) 837, procedure 2025/0360(COD)) has NOT been adopted. Its main proposals: Art. 88c, making legitimate interest an explicit basis for developing and operating AI systems, with safeguards and an unconditional right to object; a new Art. 9(2)(k) for residual special-category data in training sets; and codifying the relative identifiability of pseudonymised data from EDPS v SRB (C-413/23 P, 4 Sep 2025). As of the latest reports this track is still at Council and Parliament stage, behind the AI track.
findings.evidence: A Council presidency text (doc 12535/26) reportedly turns legitimate interest for AI training into a presumption. The EDPB and EDPS want stronger safeguards. No provisional agreement was found.

findings.claim: EU-to-US transfers to LLM APIs can still rely on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, but the risk remains open. The General Court upheld the DPF on 3 Sep 2025 (T-553/23 Latombe). Latombe appealed to the Court of Justice on 31 Oct 2025 (C-703/25 P), and no judgment had been found.
findings.evidence: The appeal asks the Court to annul the 2023 adequacy decision. The OJ notice was published 22 Dec 2025.

findings.claim: China: under Art. 2 of the 生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法 (in force 2023-08-15), the measures apply only to GenAI services offered to the public in China. Enterprises that develop or use GenAI without offering it to the public are explicitly excluded, so internal data-science agents generally need no CAC 备案. They become in scope once exposed to the public, for example through an app, mini-program or open API. Filing volume keeps growing: by 2026-08-31, 1,112 GenAI services had completed 备案 and 731 apps or features had completed local 登记 (up from 748 and 435 at 2025-12-31).
findings.evidence: Text: entities that 'develop and apply GenAI technology but do not provide services to the domestic public' are excluded. 124 services were newly filed in Jul-Aug 2026.

findings.claim: China's 人工智能生成合成内容标识办法 (CAC, MIIT, MPS and NRTA) took effect on 2025-09-01, together with a mandatory national standard on labelling methods. It requires explicit labels (visible text, sound or graphics) and implicit labels (file metadata). Providers must also add label prompts when generated text, images, audio or video are downloaded, copied or exported.
findings.evidence: Published March 2025. The mandatory GB standard was approved and implemented on the same day as the measures.

findings.claim: China's 网络数据安全管理条例 (State Council, in force 2025-01-01, 9 chapters and 64 articles) includes: Art. 19, which requires GenAI service providers to manage training-data security; Art. 18, which restricts automated tools used for collection; Art. 24, which requires deleting or anonymising unnecessary personal information collected incidentally by automated collection; and a rule that handlers of personal information on more than 10 million people follow the important-data duties in Art. 30-31 (a named data-security officer and risk assessment before providing or entrusting data).
findings.evidence: Commentators call Art. 19 the first AI-training security requirement at the level of an administrative regulation.

findings.claim: Under PIPL Art. 24, automated decisions must be transparent and fair, with no unreasonable price discrimination. Where an automated decision significantly affects someone, they may demand an explanation and refuse a decision made solely by automated means. Art. 55-56 require a prior impact assessment (PIPIA) for automated decision-making, sensitive personal information, entrusted processing and cross-border transfers, with records kept for 3 years. The 个人信息保护合规审计管理办法 (in force 2025-05-01) requires handlers of personal information on more than 10M people to audit at least every 2 years, and handlers of more than 1M to appoint a personal-information protection officer.
findings.evidence: CAC interpretation: more than 10 million people triggers an audit at least once every two years. Regulators can also order an external audit after incidents.

findings.claim: China cross-border rules (促进和规范数据跨境流动规定, in force 2024-03-22). Non-CIIO handlers are exempt below 100k people of non-sensitive personal information per calendar year. From 100k to under 1M people, or under 10k people of sensitive information, they need a standard contract or certification. Important data, 1M or more people, or 10k or more people of sensitive information require a CAC security assessment, and CIIOs always need one. FTZ negative lists can exempt further data. The 个人信息出境认证办法 (CAC/SAMR Order No. 20, issued 2025-10-14) took effect 2026-01-01 with 3-year certificates. GB/T 46068-2025 has applied since 2026-03-01. Sending Chinese personal data in prompts to an offshore LLM API counts as a transfer abroad (出境).
findings.evidence: Counts are cumulative from 1 January of the current year and exclude sensitive personal information from the 100k/1M thresholds.
sources: https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/促进和规范数据跨境流动规定/

findings.claim: China has no comprehensive AI law yet. The amended Cybersecurity Law (adopted 2025-10-28, in force 2026-01-01) adds a principle-level AI article (Art. 20) covering R&D support, training data and compute infrastructure, ethics, risk monitoring and safety oversight. The State Council's 2026 legislative plan calls to 'accelerate' comprehensive AI legislation, and the NDRC (2026-07-31) urged speeding up an 人工智能法, but no draft before the NPCSC was found. Rules keep arriving by scenario: the 人工智能拟人化互动服务管理暂行办法 (5 ministries, Order No. 21, issued 2026-04-10, in force 2026-07-15) adds security assessment, algorithm filing and AI sandboxes for companion-style services. No agent-specific CAC rule was found.
findings.evidence: CAC: the new Art. 20 makes specific provisions on AI safety and development. NPC work report (Mar 2026): strengthen legislative research on AI.

findings.claim: China financial sector: on 2026-06-18 the NFRA issued 《关于银行业保险业人工智能安全开发应用的指导意见》 (金发〔2026〕8号, 32 items). Key requirements: (1) risk tiering of AI applications and an application inventory; (2) high-risk scenarios are fund transactions, asset valuation, credit approval, underwriting and claims, and risk management; (3) high-risk uses need approval from the risk-management committee; (4) human supervision and intervention at key points; (5) emergency shutdown and manual fallback; (6) where a model is not sufficiently explainable it may only assist and a human makes the final decision; (7) raw data, reasoning paths and threshold-trigger records must be kept; (8) names, ID numbers, phone numbers and bank-card numbers must not be used to train or optimise GenAI models; (9) controls on outsourcing, concentration risk and open-source inventory; (10) Art. 25 names agent risks: data leakage, memory contamination, identity or privilege abuse, tool misuse and loss of control.
findings.evidence: Xinhua confirms 32 items covering admission control and human oversight for high-risk uses. The article-level details come from The Paper's summary.

findings.claim: China technical standards supporting GenAI filing: GB/T 45654-2025 生成式人工智能服务安全基本要求 (published 2025-04-25, in force 2025-11-01) covers training-data security, model security and security measures. It is paired with GB/T 45652 (pre-training and fine-tuning data security) and GB/T 45674 (data-annotation security), and replaces TC260-003 (2024).
findings.evidence: Mainly targets services with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity. It supports filing and testing.

findings.claim: Colorado's AI Act (SB24-205) never took effect. It was delayed to 2026-06-30 (SB25B-004), and enforcement was stayed on 2026-04-27 in a lawsuit by xAI in which the DOJ intervened. On 2026-05-14 it was repealed and replaced by SB26-189 (Colorado ADMT Act), most of which applies from 2027-01-01. The new act drops impact assessments and the duty of care. It requires: notice at the point of interaction when automated decision-making technology materially influences consequential decisions (employment, lending, insurance, health care, education, government services); a plain-language explanation within 30 days of an adverse outcome; data correction and human review or reconsideration; developer documentation (intended uses, training-data categories, limitations); and 3-year record retention. Only the AG enforces, with a 60-day cure period.
findings.evidence: Passed 34-1 in the Senate and 57-6 in the House. The AG must finish rulemaking by 2027-01-01.

findings.claim: US federal and state landscape. EO 14365 (2025-12-11) set up a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, and a White House 'National Policy Framework for AI' (Mar 2026) asks Congress to preempt 'unduly burdensome' state laws. As of Sep 2026 Congress had passed no preemption statute: the Obernolte-Trahan draft of 4 Jun 2026 stalled and leaders deferred AI bills past the midterms. State rules in force or upcoming: Texas TRAIGA (2026-01-01, mostly government use plus some banned uses); Illinois HB 3773 (2026-01-01, bans discriminatory-effect AI in employment and zip-code proxies, though its notice rules were withdrawn on 2026-06-02); California CCPA ADMT regulations (ADMT compliance by 2027-01-01, risk assessments of existing processing by end-2027).
findings.evidence: The Senate struck the 2025 10-year moratorium 99-1. The CPPA Board approved the ADMT rules on 24 Jul 2025.

findings.claim: US bank model risk management: SR 11-7 no longer applies. On 2026-04-17 the Fed, OCC and FDIC replaced it with SR 26-2 (also superseding SR 21-8) and OCC Bulletin 2026-13. The new guidance is risk-based, narrows the definition of 'model' (excluding spreadsheet arithmetic and deterministic rules), adds a section on vendor and third-party models, and is most relevant to banks with more than $30B in assets. It explicitly excludes generative and agentic AI as 'novel and rapidly evolving'. An interagency RFI on AI, including GenAI and agentic AI, was announced as coming 'in the near future'.
findings.evidence: Fed SR 26-2 page: it supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8. S&C: the guidance 'explicitly excludes generative and agentic AI models'.

findings.claim: US credit and insurance rules. The CFPB finalised Regulation B amendments on 2026-04-22, effective 2026-07-21 unless blocked in court, removing disparate-impact ('effects test') liability from Reg B and narrowing 'discouragement'. The duty under 12 CFR 1002.9 to give specific, accurate principal reasons in adverse-action notices still applies to AI and ML models. In insurance, about 25 states plus DC have adopted the NAIC AI Model Bulletin, which requires a written AI-systems governance program covering third-party models.
findings.evidence: About 64,500 comments were filed, mostly opposed, and APA challenges are expected. The NAIC map status is as of 2026-05-01. California, Colorado, New York and Texas use their own insurance AI frameworks.

findings.claim: Voluntary frameworks. NIST AI RMF is still v1.0 (2023) plus the GenAI Profile (AI 600-1, Jul 2024); a revision is under way under the AI Action Plan, but no 'RMF 2.0' or official NIST agentic profile has been published. NIST's CAISI launched an AI Agent Standards Initiative on 2026-02-17 after an RFI on agent security (prompt injection, specification gaming) that closed on 2026-03-09. A draft Cyber AI Profile (NIST IR 8596) was released in Dec 2025. ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is the certifiable AI management system standard. ISO/IEC 42006:2025 (Jul 2025) sets requirements for bodies that certify to it, and UKAS accredited BSI for 42001 certification from 2026-01-15.
findings.evidence: NIST page: the framework is being revised. CSA and Berkeley CLTC agentic profiles are not NIST products.

findings.claim: Asia-Pacific signals on agent governance. Singapore IMDA's Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (launched 2026-01-22, voluntary, updated to v1.5 in mid-2026) asks organisations to define 'significant checkpoints' where human approval is required, set chains of accountability across the agent value chain, and guard against rubber-stamp approvals. Korea's AI Basic Act took effect on 2026-01-22. It treats hiring and loan or credit evaluation as high-impact AI with human-oversight and notice duties, and defers fines (up to KRW 30M) for at least one year.
findings.evidence: IMDA case study: actions such as file edits, shell commands and network calls need approval by default.

findings.claim: Workforce: the Stanford Digital Economy Lab's August 2026 update of 'Canaries in the Coal Mine' (ADP payroll data through June 2026) finds no evidence of economy-wide job displacement. However, employment of 22-25-year-olds in AI-exposed occupations is 19% below the trend of less-exposed peers, up from 13% in the Aug 2025 version. The gap comes from reduced hiring rather than layoffs, is concentrated where AI substitutes for workers rather than complementing them, and shows no comparable gap for experienced workers. The authors present these as descriptive, not causal, results.
findings.evidence: Abstract: 'employment of young workers... now stands 19% below'. The gap has 'widened steadily since' August 2025.

findings.claim: Trust and accountability gaps are the main barrier to scaling agents. Gartner (2025-06-25) forecast that more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by end-2027 because of cost, unclear value and weak risk controls. An EY survey (Sep 2026; 202 US executives at firms with $1B+ revenue) found 98% have an AI governance policy but 47% admit bypassing it for urgent deployments. Dynatrace (Jan 2026, 919 leaders) found about half of agentic projects stuck in PoC or pilot because organisations cannot govern or validate them. The KPMG and University of Melbourne study (48,340 people in 47 countries, 2025) identifies trust as the critical adoption challenge.
findings.evidence: Gartner's survey sample was self-selected webinar attendees. Survey figures are vendor-reported.

design_implications: Add a risk-tiering gate when a use case is taken in, and keep a use-case registry. Separate (a) the agent as a development or analysis tool (ETL, data-quality checks, EDA, internal forecasting, report drafting), which is low risk in most regimes, from (b) the models or decisions the agent produces. Tag as HIGH-RISK any output used for: creditworthiness or credit scoring; life and health insurance pricing or underwriting; employment (recruiting, promotion, task allocation, performance monitoring); education access; essential services; and, under the NFRA list, fund transactions, asset valuation, credit approval, underwriting and claims, and risk management. High-risk tags trigger the heavy controls below. Korea, Colorado ADMT and California ADMT use similar 'consequential/significant decision' lists.

Minimise what reaches the LLM provider. Agents should reason over schemas, column statistics and synthetic or masked samples. Code runs inside an enterprise sandbox next to the data, and only aggregates or results go back to the model. Detect and pseudonymise PII before any prompt. Never send raw personal-information records to a third-party model. Never use customer personal data to fine-tune GenAI models; NFRA Art. 24 already prohibits this for Chinese banks and insurers.

Route models by data classification and jurisdiction through a provider-abstraction layer. Chinese personal information or important data goes to domestically deployed models: self-hosted open-weight models or filed (备案) domestic APIs. Sending it to an offshore API counts as 出境 and triggers the 100k / 1M / important-data thresholds and contract, certification or CAC-assessment duties. EU personal data goes to EU-region endpoints with zero-retention or no-training terms, and the design should not depend solely on the DPF while C-703/25 P is pending. Avoid single-vendor dependence, which NFRA flags as concentration risk.

Keep audit logs that cannot be altered. Record prompts and responses, tool calls, generated code, datasets and columns accessed (lineage), model and version IDs, parameters, approvals and who approved, and decision outputs with reasoning paths and threshold triggers (NFRA Art. 22). Retain for at least 6 months (EU AI Act Art. 26), 3 years for PIPIA records (PIPL Art. 56) and Colorado records, and longer where sector rules require. Make logs exportable for PIPL compliance audits and AI Office or market-surveillance requests.

Build human approval checkpoints into the orchestration layer, not the prompt. Require approval: (1) before accessing sensitive or personal-information datasets; (2) before any cross-border transfer; (3) before writing to production tables or systems; (4) before promoting or deploying a model; (5) before any output feeds a consequential decision; and (6) for destructive or networked tool calls (IMDA pattern). Measure reviewer override and agreement rates to catch rubber-stamping. Provide a kill switch and a manual fallback path (NFRA). Approvers should be competent and trained, as Art. 26(2) requires.

Treat the LLM as an analyst or engineer, never as the decider in high-risk flows. Train interpretable or constrained models (scorecards, monotonic GBMs, GLMs) for credit and insurance decisions, and generate per-decision reason codes (SHAP or counterfactual). These support Reg B specific-reason notices, CJEU C-203/22-style counterfactual explanations, PIPL Art. 24 explanation and refusal rights, and Colorado's 30-day adverse-outcome explanations. Where explainability is insufficient, the output is advisory only and a human makes the final decision (NFRA).

Auto-generate documentation as pipeline artifacts. Produce model cards and datasheets (intended use, training-data categories, limitations, evaluation, fairness tests, human-review instructions) matching EU AI Act Annex IV, Colorado developer documentation, and ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF evidence. Also produce draft DPIA and PIPIA templates when automated decision-making, sensitive personal information or transfers abroad are detected. This turns compliance into a product feature.

Keep fairness and bias testing built in, even though US federal disparate-impact exposure has shrunk under Reg B (effective Jul 2026). The EU, Illinois HB 3773 (zip-code proxies), the NAIC bulletin, Colorado and Korea still expect it. The AI Omnibus now permits exceptional processing of special-category data for bias detection, with safeguards; build a gated 'bias-audit enclave' for this.

Label AI output that leaves the enterprise. Add explicit and metadata labels to exported AI-generated reports, images and text (China 标识办法, in force 2025-09-01; EU Art. 50, in force 2026-08-02). Internal-only analytics can use lighter labels, but keep provenance metadata either way.

Harden agent security against the risks NFRA Art. 25 and NIST's agent RFI name: least-privilege service identities per agent, tool allowlists, read-only defaults, isolated memory per tenant and project, defences against prompt injection from data content (treat data as untrusted), egress controls, and an inventory of open-source components with vulnerability scanning.

Build vs buy. Buy or adopt the commodity layers (an LLM gateway with PII redaction, observability and eval tools, an ISO 42001-aligned GRC tool). Build the differentiating policy engine: classification-to-model routing, the approval-checkpoint orchestration, lineage-linked audit logs and the automatic compliance-artifact generator. Design it to support China, EU and US policy packs, since the rules differ in substance and timing.

Plan the roadmap around the compliance calendar: EU Art. 50 and GPAI enforcement are live (Aug 2026); Colorado ADMT, California ADMT and Korea fines arrive around Jan 2027; EU Annex III high-risk duties apply from 2 Dec 2027 and Annex I from 2 Aug 2028. For the China filing path, a public-facing deployment needs 备案 or 登记 plus GB/T 45654 security testing, and internal tools do not.

Position the product as augmenting analysts, not replacing them. Evidence shows cuts to entry-level hiring, not mass layoffs, and widespread distrust and governance gaps. Add reviewer UX, explanations of what the agent did and why, and AI-literacy onboarding (still required under EU Art. 4 in softened form). Define clear RACI ownership for every agent-produced artifact so accountability rests with a named human.
corrections_to_common_beliefs: 'EU AI Act high-risk obligations apply from 2 Aug 2026': no longer true. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (in force 2026-07-27) moved stand-alone Annex III duties to 2 Dec 2027 and Annex I to 2 Aug 2028. Art. 50 transparency duties and GPAI enforcement did start in Aug 2026.

'The Digital Omnibus legalised training AI on personal data under legitimate interest': only the AI Act track was adopted. The GDPR and data track (Art. 88c and the pseudonymisation definition) was still under negotiation as of Oct 2026.

'Colorado AI Act takes effect Feb/June 2026 with impact assessments and a duty of care': it was stayed, then repealed and replaced by SB26-189 (signed 2026-05-14). The replacement is a transparency and consumer-rights regime, mostly from 2027-01-01, with no impact assessments.
'SR 11-7 governs bank AI model risk': SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 superseded it on 2026-04-17, and the new guidance explicitly excludes generative and agentic AI, pending an RFI.

'Any enterprise use of GenAI in China needs CAC 备案': only services offered to the public in China are in scope. Internal R&D and enterprise use are excluded under Art. 2, though PIPL, the Data Security Law, the network-data regulation and cross-border rules still apply. Apps calling filed models need local 登记.

'China has a comprehensive AI Law': not yet. Only the amended Cybersecurity Law Art. 20 (in force 2026-01-01) plus scenario-specific measures exist; comprehensive legislation is in the 'accelerate' planning stage.

'Disparate-impact liability applies to AI credit models under Reg B': the CFPB removed it (final rule 2026-04-22, effective 2026-07-21, subject to litigation). Adverse-action reason requirements and state, EU and proxy-discrimination exposure remain.

'NIST AI RMF 2.0 / an official NIST agentic profile exists': AI RMF is still 1.0 plus the GenAI Profile. The revision and agent standards work are in progress; the agentic 'profiles' in circulation are from CSA and Berkeley, not NIST.

'AI is already eliminating data and analyst jobs en masse': the best payroll evidence shows no economy-wide displacement. The effect is a 19% relative shortfall in hiring of 22-25-year-olds in exposed occupations, while experienced workers are unaffected.
'The EU AI-literacy obligation requires guaranteeing staff competence': the Omnibus reframed it as taking measures to support literacy.
open_questions: Final outcome and timing of the GDPR/data track of the Digital Omnibus (Art. 88c / '88 bis' legitimate interest for AI, Art. 9(2)(k), pseudonymisation definition).

When the final Commission Article 6 high-risk classification guidelines and CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 harmonised standards will land, and whether internal data-science agents that only produce models count as 'AI systems' deployed by the enterprise.

Whether China will issue agent-specific (智能体) rules or a draft comprehensive AI law in late 2026 or 2027, and whether the NFRA approach (ban on personal information in GenAI training, assistive-only use when unexplainable) spreads to securities (CSRC), payments (PBOC) or other sectors.
Timing and content of the US interagency RFI on model risk management for generative and agentic AI, and whether any supervisory expectation for agentic AI replaces the SR 26-2 carve-out.

Litigation status of the CFPB Reg B final rule, the xAI v. Colorado case after the repeal, and DOJ AI Litigation Task Force actions against other states. Also the content of the Colorado AG's ADMT rules due by 2027-01-01.
The Court of Justice outcome in C-703/25 P (Latombe) and its effect on EU-to-US LLM API transfers.
Exact current count of NAIC bulletin adopters and of ISO/IEC 42001 certifications. Publication status of ISO/IEC 42005 (AI impact assessment) was not verified in this pass.

Whether the 1,112 filed Chinese GenAI services include enough enterprise-grade models suitable for data-science agents, for example code and SQL capability and long context, so that domestic-only deployments do not sacrifice quality.

dimension: Real enterprise case studies (2024-2026) of AI agents in analytics, data science and data engineering: what worked, measured outcomes, architecture patterns

findings.claim: OpenAI's in-house data agent (blog 'Inside our in-house data agent', Jan 29 2026, Bonnie Xu, Aravind Suresh, Emma Tang) is an internal-only analytics agent. It is built on six context layers: table usage, human annotations, Codex enrichment, institutional knowledge, memory and runtime context. Scale at launch was ~600 PB, ~70k datasets and ~3.5k internal users.
findings.evidence: A nightly Codex job reads the pipeline code behind each table to infer purpose, grain, keys, freshness and alternate tables. This catches near-duplicate tables, e.g. one that includes logged-out users and one that does not. Memory stores user corrections at global and personal scope. In one test, memory cut a question from more than 22 min to 1 min 22 s. Access goes through Slack, the web, IDEs, and Codex CLI or ChatGPT via MCP.
findings.as_of: 2026-01-29 (primary page returned 403; details from consistent secondary summaries)

findings.claim: OpenAI evaluates its data agent continuously against curated question/golden-SQL pairs. Grading compares executed results and SQL structure, not strings. Users get their own permissions passed through: the agent can query only tables the user can already access.
findings.evidence: The generated SQL is run and its output compared with the golden query's output. An OpenAI Evals grader scores each case with an explanation. The evals run like unit tests and serve as production canaries, because 'quality can drift just as easily as it can improve.' The agent flags missing access or falls back to authorized datasets. Each answer states its assumptions and links to the underlying results.

findings.claim: In OpenAI's later disclosure (May/June 2026), the agent runs on one model (GPT-5.5), with no router and no fine-tuning, and a curated set of 13 non-overlapping tools, down from about 40. Scale had grown to ~1.5 EB, ~90k datasets and ~4,000 users. The team named several things that failed.
findings.evidence: Overlapping tools caused wrong tool choices and conflicting answers. Indexing all historical queries failed because most are exploratory one-offs, so trusted dashboard queries are now ranked higher. Prescriptive step-by-step prompts did worse than high-level goals. The team's lesson: the data foundation (monorepo, annotations) matters more than the agent. Codex also helped migrate ~10k DAGs and 600 PB across clouds in about 2 months.
findings.as_of: 2026-06-03 (ByteByteGo interview with Emma Tang; user counts inconsistent within article: 4,000 vs 5,500)

findings.claim: Vercel replaced the 17 specialized tools in its internal text-to-SQL agent d0 with one sandboxed bash or file-system tool (plus ExecuteSQL), pointed at a Cube semantic layer stored as YAML, Markdown and JSON files. Every metric improved, but the eval set had only 5 queries.
findings.evidence: Success rate went from 4/5 to 5/5. Average time fell from 274.8 s to 77.4 s (3.5x faster), tokens from ~102k to ~61k (-37%), and steps from ~12 to ~7 (-42%). The model was Claude Opus 4.5 via the AI SDK. Vercel says the approach depends on a 'well-documented, consistently named semantic layer.' Author Andrew Qu, Dec 22 2025.

findings.claim: Uber's QueryGPT (Sep 2024) narrows the schema with curated domain 'workspaces' (SQL samples plus tables) and splits work into narrow LLM steps: an intent agent, a table agent where the user confirms the tables, and a column-pruning agent. In a limited release it cut query authoring from ~10 min to ~3 min.
findings.evidence: About 300 DAU in a limited release to Ops and Support. 78% of surveyed users reported time saved. The eval golden set came from real logs and was run two ways: 'Vanilla' end-to-end and 'Decoupled' with human-given intent and tables. Signals were intent accuracy, table overlap, whether the query ran, whether it returned rows, and LLM-scored similarity, with ~5% run-to-run noise ignored. Hallucinated tables and columns were still unsolved. Schemas with 200+ columns (40-60k tokens) forced column pruning.

findings.claim: Uber's Finch (Jul 2025) is a finance data agent in Slack. Instead of pointing the LLM at raw warehouse tables, it uses curated single-table data marts and an OpenSearch index of column and value aliases.
findings.evidence: A LangGraph supervisor routes requests to a SQL Writer agent, which checks RBAC before execution. Each sub-agent is evaluated separately. SQL is graded on golden-query results, not query text, and historical queries are re-run as regression tests before any prompt or model change. Human validation is planned for executive-level questions. No accuracy numbers were published.

findings.claim: LinkedIn's SQL Bot, built into the DARWIN platform on LangGraph, depends on human certification of datasets and a knowledge graph (DataHub metadata, query logs, wikis, certified notebooks). Its headline accuracy depends heavily on how it is measured.
findings.evidence: Domain experts certified hundreds of tables. An LLM re-ranker picks 7 of the top 20 tables, and EXPLAIN plus existence checks feed a self-correction step. The benchmark has 130+ questions across 10 product areas and is reviewed quarterly. About 60% of questions have multiple accepted answers; without them, recall was under-reported by 10-15%. The LLM judge lands within 1 point of humans about 75% of the time. In a survey, ~95% rated accuracy 'Passes' or better, but the KDD'25 paper found only 53% of answers correct or close on expert review. Embedding the tool in DARWIN raised adoption 5-10x, and 'Fix with AI' accounts for ~80% of sessions. The paper reports 300+ weekly users.

findings.claim: Pinterest's text-to-SQL in Querybook (2024) showed that table documentation, not the model, drives table retrieval. Only top-tier standardized tables were indexed, and users confirm the chosen tables before SQL is generated.
findings.evidence: Table-search hit rate was 40% without documentation in the embeddings and rose roughly linearly to 90% as documentation weight increased. First-shot SQL acceptance rose from 20% to over 40%. SQL-writing tasks finished ~35% faster, uncontrolled for difficulty. Spider scores did not reflect real task difficulty, and generated SQL was not validated before reaching users.

findings.claim: Pinterest's 2026 Analytics Agent sits on a DataHub context layer and 'unified context-intent embeddings'. Historical SQL is enriched with glossary terms and metric definitions, an LLM translates it into the business question it answers, and that text is embedded. Ranking combines usage signals with governance signals such as tier, freshness and documentation quality.
findings.evidence: Scale: 100k+ tables, after a multi-year cleanup from 400k, and 2,500+ analysts. AI-generated documentation cut manual documentation effort ~40%. Join-pattern analysis propagated glossary terms to more than 40% of columns. Tools are exposed via MCP and SQL is run and validated on Presto. Reported usage is '10x the usage of any other internal tool.' Humans stay in the loop for the most critical assets.
findings.as_of: ~2026-03 (Medium original returned 403; figures via DataHub and DevDay summaries)

findings.claim: Meta's home-grown Analytics Agent began as one data scientist's devserver prototype and reached weekly use by 77% of Meta's data scientists and data engineers within about 6 months. Its key design choice is personalized context mined from each user's query history.
findings.evidence: Meta found that 88% of data-scientist queries use only tables the person accessed in the preceding 90 days. Knowledge is organized as Cookbooks (domain entry points), Recipes (workflows, rules and validation) and Ingredients (semantic models, wikis, memories). Every result shows its SQL. The community created 4,500+ recipes, used 150k times. No accuracy figures were published.

findings.claim: In a talk, a Meta AI and data infrastructure director described three phases. Prompt engineering plateaued, and stronger models briefly helped then stalled. The real step-function gain came from tools for reach plus structured context (semantic models, verified queries, caveats) for truth.
findings.evidence: Stronger models stalled because better reasoning over wrong data yields 'confident wrong answers.' Reported figures: agent queries up 30x in 6 months, 60% of non-data staff using data agents weekly, and 67% of dashboard creation moved to agent-built apps within 4 months. Evaluation used a benchmark pass rate plus 'pass per key', which checks that the same question gets the same answer.

findings.claim: Grab gives the clearest public business-outcome metrics for an analytics agent program. Its Slack agent Spartan has 50+ skills and 120 analysis frameworks. Scarlet does root-cause analysis on pipeline failures and fixes or escalates them. ContextIQ manages context as a lifecycle and folds in fixes from production agent failures.
findings.evidence: Analysts' share of mechanical tickets fell from 44% (Feb) to 30% (Jun). Self-serve resolution without humans rose from 50% to 81% for SQL requests, 63% to 90% for data pulls, and 53% to 67% for metric requests. 85% of threads get a first response within 1 minute. Assets behind this: 5,000+ certified tables and metrics, ~4,000 context docs, ~2,000 golden records. A five-level autonomy ladder is applied per workflow; at L4, humans review at gates such as anomalies, novel scope or sensitive cuts.

findings.claim: Ramp Research, an internal Slack analyst agent, replaced a single on-call analyst channel and drew far more questions. Ramp's evaluation lessons are concrete: checking every answer by hand recreates the bottleneck, and end-to-end tests alone do not explain failures.
findings.evidence: 1,800+ questions across 1,200+ conversations from 300 users. In four weeks: 1,476 questions in the agent channel versus 66 in #help-data (~22x). Context comes from dbt, Looker and Snowflake metadata plus domain-owner docs kept as a file system. Tools inspect row-level values and can backtrack. A Python mini-framework in the dbt repo checks expected tool calls, table references and query shape. The agent has no PII access.
findings.as_of: launched Aug 2025 per ZenML (Ramp post excerpt undated)

findings.claim: Anthropic's Data Infrastructure team uses Claude Code for routine data-engineering work (e.g. new pipelines that follow existing patterns), Kubernetes debugging, onboarding to pipeline dependencies, and plain-text workflow files that let non-coding finance staff run data workflows. It recommends MCP servers over the BigQuery CLI for control over sensitive data.
findings.evidence: Plain-text workflows read like 'query this dashboard... run these queries, produce Excel output.' Detailed CLAUDE.md files improve results, and Claude Code monitors anomalies across ~200 dashboards. Source: Anthropic's 'How Anthropic teams use Claude Code' PDF.

findings.claim: Kuaishou's internal DataAgent is the largest Chinese case with usage metrics, disclosed at a tech salon on 2026-09-19. It moved from fixed workflows (H1 2025) to an Agentic+Skill architecture (late 2025 to Q1 2026). Accuracy figures were not disclosed.
findings.evidence: WAU above 10,600, 55 conversations per person per week, more than 80% penetration among analysts and product/ops staff, NPS 73.5, median 13x efficiency per task. Use cases: data pulls and analysis, reports, data development and ops, A/B analysis (/abtestSkill), tracking instrumentation. In e-commerce it took iteration to go from off-target answers to accurate Q&A, driven by knowledge-base work, data-pull skills and an accuracy-assurance system.

findings.claim: China's data-agent products are DataWorks Data Agent (Alibaba Cloud), Quick BI 智能小Q (Lingyang/Alibaba) and Volcano Engine Data Agent (ByteDance). They publish efficiency claims but no audited accuracy figures, and no internal ByteDance, Meituan or Ant case with metrics turned up.
findings.evidence: DataWorks claims Taobao Shangou (淘宝闪购) metric development fell from 6-8 h to 5-10 min (Apr 2026). Quick BI claims 98% and 98.2% accuracy in vendor-community articles. Volcano Engine claims 89.7% intent-recognition accuracy and +300% lead conversion with unnamed customers. One Aliyun community article argues that agents succeed only when a scenario has a defined cycle, owner, data boundary, deliverable and acceptance criteria.

findings.claim: DABstep (Adyen and Hugging Face, Feb 2025) is a benchmark of 450+ tasks taken from real payments-analyst work, combining data files with a business-rules manual. Multi-step data-agent reasoning on it remains weak.
findings.evidence: In the paper, the best agent scored 14.55% on Hard versus 76.39% on Easy (o4-mini). In the blog, o3-mini scored ~16% on Hard and Claude Sonnet ~12%. Reasoning models scored 0% under a standard ReAct prompt. Cost ranged from ~$0.004 to ~$0.97 per task. A 2026 paper reports credible leaderboard Hard scores of about 20-26%; this is unverified on the live leaderboard.

findings.claim: A Sep 2026 ablation on DABstep (arXiv 2609.22259) separated the three parts of a context layer. Semantic content (written definitions of metrics and columns) does most of the work, retrieval scaffolding adds less, and precomputed macros help only where the agent can't derive a metric. Governance rules enforced by tools blocked destructive writes.
findings.evidence: Hard-task accuracy rose from 13.9% to 55.1%, 22.6% to 56.6%, 22.9% to 68.4% and 37.0% to 77.4% across four models. Scaffolding alone added 0-5 points on flash models and 14-15 points on frontier models. Pasting the same knowledge into a 24k-character prompt was much weaker than a fetchable contract. Ungoverned setups issued 166 mutating statements and corrupted the warehouse twice; governed setups issued none. The paper also reports MotherDuck's context Guides adding +72 points on DABstep.

findings.claim: Platform vendors now ship the verified-query eval loop as a product feature. Snowflake Cortex Analyst evaluations use a semantic view's verified queries as ground truth and test against a holdout copy. They also track regressions and pin judge-model versions.
findings.evidence: Each run uses a temporary semantic view with the test verified queries removed. Correctness comes from executing the generated SQL and comparing results. The run counts regressions (queries that passed before and now fail). Metric versions v1-v3 pin the judge. Snowflake recommends several runs to set a normal range and now points new work to Cortex Agents.

findings.claim: Few published cases report correctness. Most report adoption or speed. Among them, Meta and OpenAI give no accuracy rates, Finch gives none, and Kuaishou withholds accuracy. LinkedIn's expert benchmark (53%) and Pinterest's acceptance rate (40%+) are the rare honest ones.
findings.evidence: ZenML on Meta: 'Adoption figures don't show how much analytical work the agent actually completes correctly.' The OpenAI write-up reports no accuracy or failure rates for its 'days to minutes' claim.

design_implications: Build the context layer before the agent. Every success had a curated layer first: certified and tiered tables (LinkedIn, Pinterest, Grab's 5,000+ certified assets), metric definitions or a semantic layer (Vercel Cube, Finch single-table marts, Meta Recipes), and golden or verified queries (Grab ~2,000, OpenAI, Snowflake). Budget most of the effort for this, and treat it as an ongoing lifecycle with an owner (Grab ContextIQ, LinkedIn quarterly benchmark review). It is not a one-time setup.

Add an offline enrichment pipeline. Use a coding agent to read pipeline code and lineage nightly and write table purpose, grain, keys, freshness and caveats (OpenAI Codex enrichment). Have an LLM translate historical SQL into business intent and embed that (Pinterest). Rank queries by trust (dashboard or golden over ad hoc) instead of indexing every query log.

Keep the online loop simple: one strong model, a small set of non-overlapping tools (~1-13), and file-system or bash access over semantic-layer files in a sandbox (Vercel, OpenAI). Give goals, not step-by-step procedures. Use workflow orchestration (LangGraph supervisor, Uber-style specialized steps) only where per-step evaluation or RBAC requires it.

Package domain knowledge as skills or recipes owned by domain experts (Meta Cookbooks/Recipes/Ingredients, Grab Spartan's 50+ skills, Kuaishou Agentic+Skill, Anthropic plain-text workflows and CLAUDE.md). Let teams contribute without going through the platform team.

Personalize retrieval: default to the tables and domains a user touched recently or that their org owns (Meta: 88% of queries use tables from the prior 90 days; LinkedIn org-chart and ICA defaults). This is a cheap and large gain for ambiguous questions.

Evaluation harness requirements: golden question sets drawn from real logs with multiple accepted answers; grading by executed-result comparison, not SQL string match; holdout so verified queries can't leak into generation; component-level and intermediate-step checks (Uber Decoupled mode, Ramp's dbt mini-framework); consistency checks (Meta pass-per-key); regression gates before any model or prompt change; production canaries. Accept ~5% run-to-run noise.

Governance by construction: pass the user's identity and permissions through, check RBAC before executing (OpenAI, Finch); exclude PII (Ramp); use read-only governed tools via MCP rather than raw CLIs (Anthropic). Enforce rules in the tool layer, not only in prompts: ungoverned agents issued 166 mutating statements and corrupted a warehouse twice in the DABstep ablation.

Deliver inside existing workflows (Slack, SQL editor, IDE, notebooks): LinkedIn saw 5-10x adoption when embedded in DARWIN. Show SQL, assumptions and links to results so users can verify. Turn corrections into reviewable memory.

Start with a narrow persona and high-ROI, checkable tasks such as fixing or debugging queries, metric lookups, data pulls and pipeline-failure root cause. Then climb an autonomy ladder per workflow (Grab L2 to L5), with human gates for executive, sensitive or novel-scope outputs.

Measure business value with operational KPIs, not DAU alone: self-serve resolution rate (Grab: SQL 50% to 81%), share of mechanical tickets, question volume versus the old help channel (Ramp ~22x), time per task (Uber 10 to 3 min; Kuaishou median 13x), plus an expert-graded correctness rate on a fixed benchmark.

Build vs buy: the agent loop and text-to-SQL are commoditizing (Snowflake Cortex Agents and Analyst, DataWorks Data Agent, Quick BI, Volcano Data Agent). Buy or reuse platform-native semantic layers, eval and agent runtimes where the warehouse already lives. Build the enterprise-specific context assets, evals, skills and governance glue, which is where the cases show the advantage. Require a POC on your own question set before accepting any vendor accuracy number (e.g. Quick BI's '98%').

For the data-engineering side (pipeline building and ops), the evidence is thinner but positive for bounded tasks: OpenAI migrated ~10k DAGs with Codex plus validation skills; Grab's Scarlet does pipeline root cause and escalates outside its runbooks; Anthropic builds new pipelines from existing patterns; DataWorks claims hours to minutes for metric development. Put agent-written pipelines through CI, tests and review gates, since shared-cluster risk is flagged by OpenAI.
corrections_to_common_beliefs: 'Vercel d0 reached 100% accuracy' rests on a 5-query eval (4/5 to 5/5). The robust takeaways are the latency, token and step reductions, and the dependence on a clean semantic layer, not the accuracy level.
LinkedIn SQL Bot's '95% accuracy' is a user survey ('Passes' or better). Its KDD'25 paper reports 53% correct or close on an expert-reviewed benchmark.

OpenAI data agent figures have changed over time. Jan 2026: ~600 PB, ~70k datasets, ~3.5k users, GPT-5.2. May/Jun 2026: ~1.5 EB, ~90k datasets, ~4k users, GPT-5.5, 13 tools (down from ~40). Older summaries are stale.

Better models alone do not fix enterprise analytics agents. Meta saw upgrades stall into 'confident wrong answers' until structured context was added. Stronger models do, however, make heavy scaffolding and prescriptive prompts a liability (Vercel, OpenAI). The bottleneck is semantic content, not orchestration complexity.

Public text-to-SQL benchmarks (Spider, BIRD) overstate enterprise readiness. Pinterest found real tasks much harder than Spider, and DABstep Hard tasks stayed around 15-26% for general agents. Large gains came only with domain context (e.g. 13.9% to 55.1%).

Multi-agent pipelines with many specialized tools are not best practice by default. OpenAI and Vercel both cut tools sharply and improved, while Uber's decomposition is justified mainly by per-step evaluability and schema size.
'Index all query history for RAG' is an anti-pattern. Most queries are exploratory one-offs (OpenAI), so trusted queries should be ranked higher or the index personalized (Meta).
'Human-in-the-loop on every answer' does not scale. It recreated the bottleneck at Ramp. Use sampling, gates by risk or novelty (Grab), and intermediate-step evals instead.

Chinese vendor accuracy claims (Quick BI 98%, Volcano 89.7%) are unaudited marketing numbers with unclear denominators. Internal ByteDance, Meituan and Ant data-agent metrics were not found publicly; Kuaishou (Sep 2026) is the best-documented Chinese internal case, and it does not disclose accuracy.
open_questions: OpenAI's primary blog (openai.com/index/inside-our-in-house-data-agent) returned 403. Its details come from multiple consistent secondaries (The Decoder, ZenML, ByteByteGo) and should be spot-checked against the original.

No primary public case studies were found for Netflix, Airbnb, Shopify or Block/goose internal data agents. An Airbnb job posting mentions an 'AI agent for Data' with ~7,000 MAU of analytics products, unverified. The shared web-search budget ran out before deeper searches on Airbnb, Netflix, Databricks Genie customer metrics and Spider 2.0 leaderboard status.

Meituan, ByteDance (internal) and Ant data-agent disclosures with metrics were not found. tech.meituan.com and DataFun/QCon talks should be searched directly. Meituan's 2026 work appears to focus on a metric-platform-centric BI architecture, which is a prerequisite for agents.
Accuracy versus adoption: most cases publish adoption only. What are realistic production correctness rates on expert-graded internal benchmarks at Grab, Meta, OpenAI and Kuaishou?
Cost and warehouse load from agent-generated query volume (Meta flags it), and how teams budget compute per answer.
Memory governance: how stale or conflicting memories and user corrections are reviewed, expired or promoted to global context (OpenAI leaves this unexplained).
The Gartner prediction that 40% or more of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027 (June 2025) could not be re-verified here (403 on the press release).

dimension: Empirical reliability of data/DS agents: benchmarks and measured failure modes (as of Oct 2026)

findings.claim: Spider 2.0 leaderboard (Oct 2026). Snow top score is 96.70 (Genloop Sentinel Agent v2 Pro). Lite top is 76.23 (Tencent Tianqiong Data Agent + GLM 5.2). DBT top is 65.6 (SignalPilot). Most GPT-5-class Spider2-DBT agents score 35-41. Five of the top-10 Snow entries come from China-based teams (DAQUV, Tencent, ByteDance). Paytm, an Indian firm, is also in the top 10.
findings.evidence: Snow #2 Native mini 96.53, #3 DAQUV QUVI-3 + Gemini-3-pro 94.15, #4 Tencent TCDataAgent 93.97, #8 AT&T+RelationalAI KG 86.28. Lite: DecisionX 74.95, Snowflake DivSkill-SQL 73.13, Oracle SOMA-SQL 72.02. DBT: Databao (JetBrains) 60.29, Shadowfax+GPT-5 41.18. The original 2024 baseline was GPT-4 at about 6% overall (DailSQL+GPT-4: 5.6 on Lite, 2.2 on Snow). The leaderboard lists no per-entry dates.

findings.claim: Headline text-to-SQL leaderboard numbers are partly measuring benchmark artifacts. A PVLDB audit found 62.8% annotation errors in Spider 2.0-Snow (121 examples with public gold SQL) and 52.8% in BIRD Mini-Dev. Spider2 has also published all examples and gold answers for self-evaluation since 2024-12-24. Snow scores above 90% therefore probably reflect fitting to the gold answers' conventions, not real enterprise accuracy.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2601.08778 v3 (19 Jan 2026). On corrected BIRD Dev subsets, 16 agents' scores changed by -7% to +31% (relative) and ranks moved by -9 to +9. The Spider2 README says 'release all examples and gold answers for self-evaluation' (2024-12-24). The inference about Snow scores is mine.

findings.claim: On BIRD, single-turn text-to-SQL on curated public databases has reached about 80-83% test execution accuracy. Humans score 92.96. The main gains came from generating many candidates and selecting among them. Selection is now the bottleneck: the best candidate is often in the pool but is not picked.
findings.evidence: Top test EX: GrainSQL 82.95 (Sep 2026), Huawei DataGallery 82.39, Tencent SiriusAI 82.28, Ant Agentar-Scale-SQL 81.67. Single-model track: Gemini-SQL2 80.04, using many-candidate self-consistency. On the BIRD dev set, CHASE-SQL with Gemini 1.5 Pro scored 63.01 single-query, 68.84 with self-consistency, and 82.79 if an oracle picked the best candidate.

findings.claim: Accuracy collapses once tasks become ambiguous and interactive, or use real enterprise warehouses. On BIRD-Interact (ICLR 2026 Oral), GPT-5 completes 8.67% of tasks in the conversational setting (c-Interact) and 17.00% in the agentic setting (a-Interact). On BEAVER, built from private enterprise warehouses, state-of-the-art agentic frameworks with GPT-5.2 reach 10.8% execution accuracy, and 30.1% even with oracle subtask hints.
findings.evidence: BIRD-Interact-Full has 600 tasks with up to 11,796 interactions (arXiv 2510.05318 v3, 24 Mar 2026). LiveSQLBench-Large-v1 (3 Mar 2026) adds 'Business Rule Drift' at about 1K columns. BEAVER v3 (13 May 2026) has 9,128 question-SQL pairs over 812 tables in 19 domains.

findings.claim: DABstep (Adyen/Hugging Face, 450 multi-step financial-analysis questions). Hard-split accuracy on the validated leaderboard rose from 14.55% at launch to 89.95%. The winning recipe was an offline, curated, reusable function library, not a bigger model at inference. Validation is now closed: the unvalidated board is full of 100% entries, including ones named 'test gold' and 'Spoofer'. DABStep-v2 is pending.
findings.evidence: Validated board: NVIDIA KGMON (NeMo Agent Toolkit) scores 89.95 hard / 87.5 easy (22 Feb 2026). It used Claude Haiku 4.5 at inference, with a helper.py library refactored by Opus 4.5/4.6 against dev-split ground truth plus offline reflection. Its Claude Code + Opus baseline scored 66.93. OceanBase/Ant DataPilot (Qwen3) 87.57; Google DS-STAR 45.24; Claude 4 Sonnet ReAct baseline 19.84. The space says validation requests are closed.

findings.claim: On MLE-bench (75 Kaggle competitions, 24h budget), top agents now medal on about 61-64% of all competitions and 77-80% of the Low/Lite split (22 competitions). High-complexity competitions sit at about 40-47%. The official leaderboard has stopped taking new submissions, and v1 has known dataset issues.
findings.evidence: Famou-Agent 2.0 + Gemini-3-Pro: 64.44 all / 80.3 low / 42.22 high (2026-02-23). AIBuildAI + Claude-Opus-4.6: 63.11 all, best high split at 46.67. MLEvolve 61.33 on a 12h budget. The Oct 2024 AIDE + o1-preview baseline was 17.12. Disarray (77.78) is flagged for test-set feedback and listed as not comparable. Known label leakage exists (e.g., random-acts-of-pizza), and a v2 is planned.

findings.claim: End-to-end data-lake pipelines remain a weak spot. On KramaBench (ICLR 2026), the best system reaches 55% end-to-end, and only 62% even with perfect retrieval. LLMs identify up to 42% of the important data tasks but fully implement only 20% of individual subtasks. A later auditable runtime (RADAR) reports 0.723 overall.
findings.evidence: KramaBench has 104 pipelines over 1,700 files, 24 sources and 6 domains (v3, 5 Mar 2026). RADAR (arXiv 2609.32528, 26 Sep 2026) reports 0.723 with full source retrieval and 0.747 with gold sources supplied: +35.9% and +28.8% relative over the strongest baseline.

findings.claim: Data engineering (ELT/dbt) has split in two: extraction and loading are largely solved, but transformation and modeling are not. Repeat-run consistency (Pass^3) sits 8-16 points below Pass@1, which matters for production pipelines.
findings.evidence: ELT-Bench-Verified (Apr 2026), SWE-Agent with Sonnet 4.5: EL 96% (up from 37% with Sonnet 3.5). Transformation 22.66%, rising to 32.51% after benchmark fixes. 82.7% (67/81) of failed transformation tasks had benchmark-attributable errors. Among unmatched columns, agent errors were mostly flawed SQL logic (33.5%) and JOIN-type errors (23.8%). Snowflake data-eng-bench (6 Aug 2026; 103 dbt tasks, 579 tables): CoCo + Opus 5 Pass@1 73.8 / Pass^3 64.1; Sonnet 5 56.6 / 40.8; Claude Code + Opus 5 69.6 / 60.2 at 3.9x the cost (a vendor-run benchmark).

findings.claim: ADE-bench (dbt Labs with Benn Stancil, Apr 2026) found that context and configuration mattered more than model choice. Agents fix syntax and logic bugs well. They struggle with data-level problems (bad values, wrong filter strings, inconsistent entity states) unless they actually query the data. Early wrong turns compound.
findings.evidence: The dbt blog (15 Apr 2026) dropped its planned model leaderboard for this reason. It notes that agents found the intended issue but also made unrequested changes when prompts were vague. Vendor-reported ADE-bench results (Paradime, 43 tasks): DinoAI 88.37%, Claude Code baseline 39.53%. These are not independently verified, and the task set has since grown to 65.

findings.claim: Older data-science agent benchmarks (2024-25 models) put realistic multi-step analysis accuracy at about 30-35%. ScienceAgentBench has plateaued at about 30-33% even with 2025 frontier models, and the scaffold changes results more than the model does.
findings.evidence: DSBench (ICLR 2025): 34.12% on 466 analysis tasks. DA-Code (EMNLP 2024): 30.5% on 500 tasks. HAL ScienceAgentBench: o3 + self-debug 33.33%; Sonnet 4.5 and GPT-5 30.39%. The same Claude-3.7 Sonnet scores 30.39% in the self-debug scaffold but 17.65% in the HAL generalist agent, at about 4x the cost. HAL notes cost figures inflated up to 2x (5 Oct 2026).
