I did not check for 2026 re-runs of DSBench or DA-Code.

findings.claim: Curated semantics (a semantic layer, knowledge graph or metric definitions) consistently adds about 8-25 points of text-to-SQL accuracy. Its biggest value is turning plausible wrong answers into explicit 'cannot answer' errors. The independent effect size at moderate scale is about +20 points, not the 3-5x that vendors claim.
findings.evidence: dbt (7 Apr 2026; 11 questions x 20 runs): on the modeled schema, Sonnet 4.6 scores 90.0% text-to-SQL vs 98.2% semantic layer, and GPT-5.3-codex 84.1% vs 100%. On the unmodeled schema, text-to-SQL scores 64.5% vs 72.7% for the semantic layer, and out-of-scope questions return errors rather than wrong data. Independent paired benchmark (arXiv 2604.25149, 100 questions, Opus 4.7 / Sonnet 4.6 / GPT-5.4): 67.7-68.7% with the semantic layer vs 45.5-50.5% without, +17 to +23 pp, p<0.01. data.world: 16% raw SQL, 54% with a knowledge graph, then 72% correct + 8% 'I don't know' + 20% wrong with ontology query checks and repair (2024). AtScale (vendor, 40 questions): 20% to 92.5%.

findings.claim: Retrieving historical-query context (SQL 'reference cards') gives only small, statistically insignificant gains on the public enterprise benchmark (BEAVER). The gains were larger on an in-house production set. Context engineering does not substitute for curated semantics.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2608.22830 (24 Aug 2026). An internal set of 5,176 production queries from an online retailer gained about 12-25% in SQL AST similarity. On BEAVER, the best variant scored 9.00% vs a 6.33% baseline (N=300, p=0.12).

findings.claim: Most data-agent failures are silent: the agent returns a normal-looking but wrong answer rather than crashing. Iterative self-verification does not eliminate this. An auditable runtime with typed operators and runtime validation reduced silent errors by 28.6%.
findings.evidence: RADAR (arXiv 2609.32528, Sep 2026) tested 1,054 tasks across KramaBench, DA-Code and DABStep. For the DS-STAR baseline, 405 of 580 zero-score runs (69.8%) returned normal-looking wrong results, against 84 non-deliveries. RADAR cut silent errors to 289 and non-deliveries to 24. The paper notes silent errors persist even with iterative verification. ToxicBench (arXiv 2609.37153): plausible but poisoned tool outputs cut task success by 26-39 pp. The CMBAgent astrophysics study names silent incorrect computation as the dominant failure.

findings.claim: LLM-as-judge without running the code is unreliable for verifying code and SQL. The best code judge reaches about 82%. Accuracy swings by up to 14% when the order of the two responses is swapped. Pairwise judging clearly beats pointwise scoring. Execution-match metrics also have material false positives and negatives.
findings.evidence: CodeJudgeBench (ACL 2026): Gemini-2.5-Pro averages 82.12% (codegen 81.98, repair 84.93, unit tests 79.46). Order-swap discrepancies reach up to 14%. QwQ-32B gets 46% 'correct' pointwise vs 76.89% pairwise (my calculation from two tables), with 'significant randomness'. FLEX (NAACL 2025): an LLM judge given full context raised agreement with experts (Cohen's kappa) from 62 to 87.04. Re-scoring leaderboards gave -3.15 average from false positives and +6.07 from false negatives.

findings.claim: Verifiers that interact with the execution environment measurably beat text-only verifiers on data tasks. DataPRM (KDD 2026), a 4B process reward model that probes intermediate execution states, finds silent errors that general reward models miss. It improves best-of-N results on ScienceAgentBench and DABStep.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2604.24198 (v2 20 Jun 2026): best-of-N +7.21% on ScienceAgentBench and +11.28% on DABStep. RL with DataPRM reached 78.73% on DABench and 64.84% on TableBench. General PRMs judge code text, not execution semantics.

findings.claim: In multi-agent setups, majority voting provides most of the gain usually credited to debate. Vanilla debate does not improve expected correctness. Consensus-based selectors can also agree on the same hallucination.
findings.evidence: 'Debate or Vote' (Choi, Zhu, Li; NeurIPS 2025 spotlight): across 7 NLP benchmarks, voting accounts for most of the gains, and debate induces a martingale over agents' beliefs. Debate helps only with interventions that bias updates toward correction. DPC (ACL 2026) attributes self-consistency and LLM-judge failures to 'consensus on hallucinations' and reports gains of at most 2.2 pp from better selection.

findings.claim: Reliability is lagging accuracy. In HAL's study of 14 models across 24 months, accuracy kept rising while reliability (consistency across runs, robustness to paraphrased prompts, predictability) improved only slightly. The gap between 'solves it at least once' (pass@k) and 'solves it every time' (pass^k) is substantial for every model.
findings.evidence: 'Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability' (arXiv 2602.16666, ICML 2026) on GAIA and tau-bench. Consistency often does not improve with model size. Prompt robustness is the main differentiator between models. HAL paused new leaderboard models to focus on reliability. This matches the 8-16 pt Pass@1 vs Pass^3 gaps in Snowflake's data-eng-bench.

findings.claim: Benchmark answer keys are themselves a major error source, and errors cut in both directions. Fixing ELT-Bench added about 10 pp. BIRD and Spider2 annotation errors reshuffle rankings. MLE-bench v1 has leakage. DABstep's open board was gamed. Any in-house evaluation set needs its own audit step.
findings.evidence: ELT-Bench-Verified: 22.66% to 32.51% after corrections alone, with LLM-plus-human audit at Fleiss kappa 0.85. BIRD audit: ranks moved by up to ±9. MLE-bench lists known issues and plans a v2. DABstep closed validation and is moving to v2.

design_implications: Plan around realistic accuracy by task type, not leaderboard SOTA. Text-to-SQL on curated, well-documented schemas: ~80-90%. Raw enterprise warehouses without curated context: ~10-30% (BEAVER). Ambiguous multi-turn questions: ~10-25% (BIRD-Interact). Multi-step document+data analysis: ~20-45% generic, ~85-90% with a domain-specific verified tool library (DABstep). End-to-end data-lake pipelines: ~55-72% (KramaBench). dbt/ELT transformation builds: ~23-74% Pass@1 depending on benchmark, with Pass^3 8-16 pts lower. Kaggle-style ML modeling: ~60-64% any-medal, ~80% on simpler tasks, ~40-47% on the hardest. Data-driven science: ~30-33%.

Build a curated semantic or metric layer first (dbt MetricFlow, Cube, a custom ontology), and expose it to agents as tools, e.g., via MCP. It is the best-evidenced lever: +8 to +25 pp accuracy. More importantly, it converts silent wrong answers into explicit out-of-scope errors. Route KPI, board and audited numbers only through governed metrics. Allow raw text-to-SQL only for labeled exploratory use.

Copy the DABstep winning pattern. A strong model offline distills verified, reusable domain functions (a skills or helper library) against labeled tasks. A cheap model then orchestrates those functions at runtime. The KGMON entry got about 30x lower latency with higher accuracy than a Claude Code + Opus baseline. Hold out data when building the library, to avoid overfitting like a benchmark.

Treat silent errors as the primary risk. About 70% of failures look normal. Require auditable execution: typed operators with recorded inputs and outputs, source and lineage capture, runtime validation (schema, row counts, units, invariants), and a strict ability to say 'cannot answer' or abstain. Do not rely on self-verification loops alone.

Verification stack, in order of evidence: (1) execution-grounded checks and data assertions, e.g., dbt tests and Great Expectations-style invariants; (2) multiple candidates with a learned or pairwise selector, or a majority vote; (3) verifiers that interact with the environment (DataPRM-style) for best-of-N; (4) LLM judges only as pairwise comparisons with randomized order and multiple samples, calibrated against human labels. Avoid vanilla multi-agent debate: it costs tokens without raising expected correctness.

Measure reliability, not just accuracy. Report pass^k or Pass^3 and variance across seeds and prompt paraphrases. Use a strict all-assertions-pass criterion for pipelines. Track cost per task: the same model varied 2-4x in cost across harnesses with equal or lower accuracy.

Budget for building and auditing an internal evaluation set. Public benchmarks have 30-60% answer-key error rates in places, and some leaderboards are gamed. Use an LLM-driven auditor plus human validation to clean your own gold labels, and use multiple prompt variants per task, as ADE-bench does.

For ambiguous business questions, design explicit clarification turns and business-rule glossaries (e.g., what 'account' means across teams). Interactive benchmarks show this is where current agents fail most.

Build vs buy: model choice shifts quality ~17 pts, but harness, context and configuration often matter as much (ADE-bench, the HAL scaffold gap). Buy or adopt the models and a mature harness. Build the proprietary context: semantic layer, domain tool library, evaluation set and runtime guards. That is the defensible value.

China context: China-based teams (Tencent, Ant, ByteDance, Huawei, OceanBase) and open models (GLM 5.2, Qwen3, DeepSeek-V3.2/V4) are at or near the top of Spider2-Lite, BIRD, DABstep and MLE-bench. A domestic-model stack is viable for regulated or on-prem deployment, provided the same verification layers are in place.
corrections_to_common_beliefs: 'Spider 2.0 is basically unsolved (6-20%)' is outdated. Lite is 76.23 and DBT 65.6 as of Oct 2026, and Snow shows 96.70, but Snow scores are suspect: public gold answers and a 62.8% annotation-error audit.

'DABstep Hard is about 15%' is outdated. The validated top score is 89.95% (Feb 2026), using a pre-built domain function library. The open leaderboard is now unreliable (many 100% entries, including 'test gold').
'MLE-bench medal rate is about 17%' is outdated. It is 61-64% overall and 77-80% on Lite with 24h budgets, but the board is frozen and v1 has leakage issues.
'ELT transformation is about 4% solvable' is outdated. It is 22.66% with Sonnet 4.5 and 32.51% on the corrected benchmark. Extraction and loading is about 96%.
'Leaderboard SOTA reflects enterprise accuracy' is wrong. BEAVER, built from real warehouses, gives GPT-5.2 agentic frameworks 10.8% (30.1% with oracle hints).

'A semantic layer makes LLMs 3-5x more accurate' is vendor framing on tiny question sets. Independent 2026 evidence shows +17 to +23 pp. The big structural win is refusing rather than answering wrongly.
'Multi-agent debate improves correctness' is mostly a voting effect. Debate alone is a martingale (NeurIPS 2025).
'LLM-as-judge can verify code and SQL correctness' is unreliable without execution: about 82% best accuracy, up to 14% swings from response order, and notable randomness.
'Execution accuracy equals correctness' is false. Execution-match metrics have false positives and negatives, and benchmark gold SQL is often wrong.
'Self-verification and reflection loops catch errors' is insufficient. Silent errors persist in agents with iterative verification (RADAR, Sep 2026).
'Newer and bigger models are more reliable' holds for accuracy and calibration but much less for consistency and repeatability (HAL reliability study).
open_questions: DABStep-v2 design and first results; whether validated Hard scores (~90%) generalize to held-out questions.
Whether Spider2-Snow scores above 90% survive independent re-validation after the annotation-error audit; whether Spider2 maintainers have corrected the gold answers.
Independent, large-scale (hundreds of questions, many tables) replications of semantic-layer and knowledge-graph gains; most evidence is still ≤100 questions or vendor-run.
Reliable LLM-judge accuracy specifically for data-analysis outputs and reports (as opposed to code); no direct benchmark was found.
Chinese-language enterprise text-to-SQL and data-agent benchmarks were not covered by this search; Chinese query ambiguity may change accuracy ranges.
2026 re-runs of DSBench, DA-Code, DataSciBench and BLADE with current frontier models were not verified, because the web search budget ran out. Those benchmarks' numbers here reflect 2024-25 models.
Cost-normalized reliability (pass^k per dollar) for production data pipelines; HAL flags its cost figures as inflated by up to 2x.
How far data-eng-bench's (Snowflake, vendor-run) and ADE-bench's vendor-reported results hold under neutral harness comparisons.

Includes build-vs-buy conclusion. findings.claim: Snowflake Intelligence (business-user agent app) and Cortex Agents went GA in Nov 2025. At Summit 2026 (June 1-4) Snowflake renamed Snowflake Intelligence to 'CoWork' and Cortex Code to 'CoCo'. design_implications: BUY or reuse from the incumbent platform: (a) NL-to-SQL/BI chat over governed data (CoWork, Genie Agents/Genie One, Fabric data agent, BigQuery/Looker Conversational Analytics, DataWorks ChatBI). This is commoditized and often free during promotions, so building a generic text-to-SQL chatbot has near-zero differentiation. (b) In-platform coding agents for SQL, dbt, pipelines and notebook ML (CoCo, Genie Code, BigQuery DE/DS agents, DataWorks Data Agent, dbt Wizard). (c) Governance primitives: Unity Catalog, Horizon, Purview, Knowledge Catalog, agent identity, row and column security. (d) Managed MCP servers and code sandboxes.

REUSE, don't rebuild, the semantic layer: author metrics once in the platform layer (semantic views, UC metric views, LookML, Power BI models, or MetricFlow) and keep a portable copy in MetricFlow or Apache Ossie (OSI) YAML. The pipeline should consume semantics, not invent them. Treat the dbt 'Agents Schema' and OSI as the interchange contract so an independent pipeline can read the same definitions across Snowflake, Databricks and BigQuery.

BUILD where vendors are structurally weak, which is cross-platform work. Each vendor agent sees only its own estate: the BigQuery DE agent only runs against BigQuery; the Fabric data agent fails across regions and caps answers at 25x25; Genie and CoWork are scoped to their own catalogs. A vendor-neutral orchestrator that calls each platform's agent or MCP server (Genie MCP, BigQuery MCP, Snowflake MCP, dbt MCP) and reconciles results is the independent value.

BUILD an independent verification and evaluation layer. Vendor accuracy claims (Genie Code 77.1%, Cortex Sense 83%) are self-benchmarked. Enterprises need their own golden question and SQL sets, recomputation of agent answers through a second engine or path, semantic-definition conformance checks, statistical sanity tests, and reproducible evidence bundles. Databricks buying Quotient AI shows evaluation is strategic, but a vendor evaluating its own agent is a conflict of interest.

BUILD the business-decision loop: question, analysis, recommendation, decision record, action, outcome measurement, and ROI attribution. Vendors stop at answers or simple actions (Genie One 'answers to action', Fabric operations agents, Volcano's 'task chain'). Causal/experiment design (BigQuery AI.CAUSAL_EFFECT is only Preview), decision logging and post-hoc outcome tracking remain open, and this is where measurable business value is proven.

BUILD cross-platform agent FinOps. Pricing has moved to token or credit consumption with promotions that expire: Snowflake AI Credits at $2.00/$2.20; Databricks Genie free through Jan 31, 2027 but service principals billed now; Google data agents about $3/$20 per million data tokens after the trial; DataWorks credits at ¥0.05. An automated pipeline will run as a service principal, so it pays from day one. Budget, route and attribute cost per business outcome.

Design for churn. Products are renamed or deprecated within months (Knowledge Assistant GA to legacy in 9 months, Supervisor API deprecated, Assistant to Genie Code, Intelligence to CoWork, Notebook agent to Hex agent). Integrate through stable protocols (MCP, A2A, SQL, OSI) behind an adapter layer, never through product-specific SDKs, in the pipeline core.

China and global split: use DataWorks Data Agent (Qwen, DeepSeek or GLM; skills; approval modes), Volcano Engine Data Agent or Tencent DataBuddy for China-resident data, and Snowflake/Databricks/BigQuery/Fabric abroad. The independent layer should run where data residency requires (Snowflake charges +10% for regional routing) and support swapping models; the Fabric data agent does not let you change its LLM.

AVOID building: a generic notebook copilot, a generic NL2SQL engine, your own vector or memory store when on Databricks (Lakebase-backed memory) or Snowflake, your own agent hosting runtime for single-platform agents, or a proprietary semantic format. PRIORITIZE: cross-platform verification and evidence, decision and ROI loop, policy-as-code over agent actions (approval gates like DataWorks' plan-only-to-yolo modes, used consistently across vendors), and agent cost governance.

findings.claim: The current MCP revision is 2026-07-28. It makes the protocol stateless: protocol-level sessions, the Mcp-Session-Id header and the initialize handshake are gone. Every request carries its protocol version and client capabilities in _meta, and servers must implement server/discover.
findings.evidence: The official versioning page says: 'The current protocol version is 2026-07-28.' Other changes in this revision: Multi Round-Trip Requests (InputRequiredResult) replace server-initiated sampling, elicitation and roots requests. Tasks moved into an official extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks). SSE resumability was removed. OpenTelemetry traceparent conventions were added to _meta. Servers SHOULD return tools/list in a deterministic order to help prompt caching, and list results now carry ttlMs and cacheScope. Roots, Sampling, Logging and Dynamic Client Registration are deprecated, with a removal window of at least 12 months. MCP python-sdk v2.0.0 shipped on 2026-07-28; v2.3.0 shipped on 2026-10-02.

findings.claim: Remote MCP authorization is now a full OAuth 2.1 resource-server profile. Servers MUST publish Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728). Clients MUST send RFC 8707 resource indicators, MUST validate the RFC 9207 iss parameter when it is present, and MUST NOT pass tokens through. Client ID Metadata Documents are preferred, Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated, and STDIO servers should take credentials from the environment instead.
findings.evidence: The spec says: 'MCP servers MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens.' Servers must validate that each token's audience is the server itself. DCR is 'retained for backwards compatibility' only. Scope step-up runs through 403 insufficient_scope responses.

findings.claim: The Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA) extension for MCP became stable on 2026-06-18. An admin provisions MCP server access through the corporate IdP: the client gets an ID-JAG token at SSO and exchanges it for an access token, so users never see a per-server consent screen.
findings.evidence: Okta is the first supported IdP. Clients: Anthropic (Claude, Claude Code, Cowork), with VS Code in preview. Servers include Asana, Atlassian, Figma, Linear and Supabase, and Slack is adding support. Policy is set by IdP group or role and audited centrally.

- Subagents: isolated context that returns a summary.
- Hooks: deterministic and outside the context window.

design_implications: Default architecture: one orchestrating agent with strong tools. Use read-only subagents only for context isolation, for example schema discovery, data profiling, log or incident triage and literature scans. Keep a single writer for code, DAG and SQL changes and for any production data mutation. This matches Cognition's 'writes stay single-threaded' finding and Anthropic's own guidance.

Avoid fixed-role 'AI team' designs (CEO, PM, analyst, engineer personas) and parallel-writer swarms. If you need fan-out, for example profiling 500 tables or checking 1,000 data-quality rules, hold the plan in deterministic code: a dynamic-workflow-style script or an Airflow/Dagster/Prefect DAG that calls agents with schema-validated outputs. Add an adversarial verifier step, and budget tokens explicitly, because runs of 15x or more tokens are normal.

Make code execution in a sandbox the main data-processing primitive. The agent writes pandas, Polars or SQL code that runs where the data lives and returns only summaries, aggregates or samples to the model. This cuts tokens by 37–98% and keeps PII and raw rows out of the LLM context. Expose a small set of composable tools and use tool search or deferred loading, because selection degrades beyond about 30–50 tools.

Build the data-access layer as MCP servers that target the 2026-07-28 stateless spec:
- No session affinity, so they scale behind a load balancer.
- Deterministic tools/list ordering.
- Separate read and write tools with destructive annotations.
- Server-minted handles in tool arguments for cursors or query jobs.
- OAuth 2.1 with RFC 9728/8707 and audience-bound tokens.
- Enterprise-Managed Authorization through the corporate IdP.
Do not build new features on Sampling, Roots, MCP Logging, Dynamic Client Registration or SSE resumability.

Package domain procedures as Agent Skills (SKILL.md plus scripts), for example a feature-engineering playbook, data-contract checks, model-card generation or a backfill runbook. Put repo conventions in AGENTS.md, which Claude Code also reads. These artifacts are portable across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Databricks Genie Code, Snowflake Cortex Code, TRAE and DeepSeek Deep Code. That hedges vendor and region risk, which matters in China, where Claude and OpenAI access may be restricted.

Make the harness swappable. Use Claude Agent SDK or claude -p --bare, OpenAI Agents SDK SandboxAgent, or ADK 2.0 behind your own interface, and keep tools in MCP and procedures in skills, so domestic models such as Qwen or DeepSeek can be swapped in. Pin versions: OpenAI Agents SDK is still 0.x, ADK has breaking 1.x to 2.x storage changes, and Claude Code ships near-daily.

Enforce guardrails deterministically, not through prompts:
- Hooks, for example PreToolUse to block DROP or DELETE and writes to prod schemas.
- Permission modes such as dontAsk plus --permission-prompts none in CI.
- --bare in CI so a repo's hooks and .mcp.json cannot run unvetted.
- --max-budget-usd caps.
- A network egress allowlist in the sandbox.
- Short-lived, sandbox-scoped credentials kept outside the code sandbox, following the OpenAI harness/compute split.

Sandbox choice:
- Global or managed: E2B, Modal, Cloudflare or Vercel.
- On-prem, private cloud or China: kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox with gVisor or Kata, or self-hosted E2B (Firecracker, with Terraform and single-host modes).
- Do not build on Daytona OSS, which was archived in June 2026.
For sensitive data, note that Claude programmatic tool calling and Managed Agents are not eligible for Zero Data Retention. Run your own loop with a self-hosted sandbox, or use the Managed Agents self-hosted sandbox option.

Evals as a first-class pipeline stage:
- Start with 20–50 tasks from real failures.
- Grade outcomes, for example tests pass, data-quality assertions hold, metrics stay within tolerance, or the output matches a golden table.
- Report pass^k for production automations where consistency matters.
- Keep a capability suite separate from a regression gate.
- Use a separate skeptical evaluator agent, not self-grading.

Observability: for ML teams, reuse MLflow 3.x, which already traces Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and Qwen agents, offers LLM judges, RBAC and an MCP registry, and ingests OpenTelemetry. Use self-hosted Langfuse (MIT core) where data residency matters. Use Inspect AI or Harbor for sandboxed agent benchmarks. Propagate OpenTelemetry trace context through MCP _meta so agent, tool and warehouse spans join end to end. Account for vendor consolidation: Promptfoo is now OpenAI-owned and Langfuse is ClickHouse-owned.

Use A2A only at organizational or vendor boundaries, for example calling a partner's or another business unit's agent as an opaque service. Inside your own pipeline, use function calls, subagents and MCP. A2A v1.0 is stable but not backward compatible with 0.3.

Budget for re-evaluating the scaffolding with every model upgrade. Both Anthropic and Cognition report that harness components such as sprints, context resets and planners become dead weight as models improve. Keep the harness thin and test removing parts on your eval suite.
corrections_to_common_beliefs: 'MCP is a stateful, session-based protocol with an initialize handshake' is outdated. Since 2026-07-28 MCP is stateless: no Mcp-Session-Id, no initialize, server/discover, multi round-trip requests, and tasks as an extension. Sampling, Roots and Logging are deprecated.

'Use Dynamic Client Registration for remote MCP auth' is outdated. DCR is deprecated in favor of Client ID Metadata Documents, and enterprises can use the stable Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension (IdP-issued ID-JAG, no per-server consent).

'MCP is Anthropic's protocol' is outdated. MCP, AGENTS.md, goose, A2A and agentgateway are all hosted by the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation. Agent Skills is a separate open standard that Anthropic originated.
'Claude Code only reads CLAUDE.md' is outdated. It now also reads AGENTS.md.
'Claude Code SDK / headless mode' should now be called the Claude Agent SDK. claude -p is its CLI form, and --bare is recommended for scripts and will become the default.

'Multi-agent teams of role-playing agents are the trend' is mostly hype for production. Vendors endorse narrow forms: read-only research or search subagents, clean-context reviewers, script-orchestrated fan-out with verification, and single-threaded writes. Claude Code agent teams are still experimental and disabled by default.
'Cognition says never build multi-agents' is outdated. Its April 2026 update endorses specific multi-agent flows as long as writes stay single-threaded.
'Daytona is an open-source self-hostable sandbox' is outdated. The OSS repo was archived in June 2026 and core development is now private.
'Promptfoo and Langfuse are independent OSS startups' is outdated. OpenAI agreed to acquire Promptfoo (March 2026) and ClickHouse acquired Langfuse (January 2026).
'A2A v1.2 is current' (seen in several blogs) is unverified. Primary GitHub releases show v1.0.0 (2026-03-12) and v1.0.1 (2026-05-28).
'More tools make the agent more capable' is wrong. Selection accuracy degrades beyond about 30–50 tools; use tool search, deferred loading or code-mode APIs.
Codex: the `codex mcp-server` command was removed in favor of the app server, the `untrusted` approval policy is retired, and the docs moved to learn.chatgpt.com.

Whether the official MCP Registry has reached GA, or has a stable v1 API, as of October 2026.
Real production adoption of A2A inside enterprise data platforms beyond vendor announcements, and when A2A v1.1 (task history, bidirectional streaming) will ship.
The license of Daytona's last OSS release (v0.190.0): sources conflict between AGPL-3.0 and Apache-2.0. Also what Daytona's private development means for self-hosted deployments.
Braintrust and LangSmith product status and pricing in October 2026 were not checked directly. LangSmith's SDK repo restructure (2026-10-16) is a repo split, not a product change.
The exact OpenAI model names behind Codex in October 2026 (docs mention 'GPT-6 Astra'; a blog mentions 'GPT-6.1 Sol'). This does not affect the architecture.

findings.evidence: GitHub v2.0.0 release: 'After seven betas, Pydantic AI V2 is now stable.' PyPI shows 2.0.0b1 on 2026-05-21 and 2.0.0 on 2026-06-23.

findings.claim: The other agent frameworks are in very different health. CrewAI 1.15.28 (MIT) made 289 PyPI releases in 2026, so the API churns heavily. smolagents' last release was 1.26.0 (2026-05-29), and every commit since has been CI or security hardening, so feature work has stalled. OpenHands (MIT) is very active: v1.28.1 on 2026-10-19 and openhands-sdk 1.56.0. AutoGen's last release was autogen-agentchat 0.7.5 (2025-09-30).
findings.evidence: PyPI release counts and GitHub commit logs. smolagents commits Sep-Oct 2026 are all 'Pin GitHub Actions…' or 'harden workflows'. OpenHands has 91k stars and the repo moved from All-Hands-AI to the OpenHands org.

findings.claim: The MCP layer changed generation. A new MCP protocol revision dated 2026-07-28 and Python SDK v2 shipped the same day; `mcp` is now at 2.3.0. FastMCP moved to PrefectHQ with v3.0 (2026-02-18). FastMCP 4.0 went stable on 2026-08-31, with sessionless requests that scale behind a load balancer, per-connection protocol negotiation, background tasks, interactive tools, and identity assertion and client-credentials auth for agents. The latest is 4.1.1 (2026-10-18, Apache-2.0), and 3.4.x still gets patches.
findings.evidence: FastMCP v4.0.0 notes: 'On July 28, MCP released the 2026-07-28 protocol revision and the rewritten Python SDK v2 shipped the same day.' FastMCP has 28k stars.

findings.claim: Inspect AI, from the UK AI Security Institute (MIT), is the active open-source framework for agent and LLM evaluation. It releases almost daily (0.3.281 on 2026-10-15) and is still 0.x.
findings.evidence: PyPI and GitHub releases 0.3.278 through 0.3.281 between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-15; 3k stars.

findings.claim: Lineage, monitoring and feature tooling are uneven. OpenLineage is healthy: 1.54.0 on 2026-10-13, Apache-2.0, releasing about every six weeks. Marquez, its reference UI and backend, has not released since 0.50.0 (2024-10-24), and its last commit was 2026-04-12. Evidently OSS (Apache-2.0, 'Beta') is slow: 0.7.23 on 2026-09-11, with no commits between May and Sep 2026. Feast (Apache-2.0) ships monthly, 0.67.0 on 2026-10-13. marimo (Apache-2.0) is active at 0.25.1 (2026-10-01) but still 0.x.
findings.evidence: GitHub release and commit logs; PyPI release counts for 2026 (Evidently 4, marimo 45, Feast monthly).

findings.claim: Lightweight Python-first ingestion and DAG tools are active and permissively licensed. dlt is at 1.31.0 (2026-10-07, Apache-2.0). Kedro is at 1.7.0 (2026-09-28). Hamilton has moved to the Apache incubator: install `apache-hamilton` (1.90.0) instead of `sf-hamilton`.
findings.evidence: The PyPI summary for sf-hamilton says 'This package has moved to apache-hamilton'.

corrections_to_common_beliefs: 'dbt Fusion is ELv2' is out of date. Since 2026-06-01 the Fusion source is Apache-2.0 inside dbt OSS, and the 'dbt' binary is proprietary under the dbt Product Licensing Agreement: free, no size limits, but some features need a login.

'dbt-core is the open-source dbt' needs care. The v2 open distribution is 'dbt OSS' (pip dbt-oss). `pip install dbt` has installed the proprietary Fusion binary since 2026-09-14. dbt-core 1.13 will be the last 1.x minor.
'MetricFlow is BSL / not open source' is wrong. It has been Apache-2.0 since 2025-10-14, and dbt contributed it to the OSI and Apache Ossie (incubating) effort.
'SQLMesh is a Tobiko/Fivetran product' is out of date. It has been a Linux Foundation project since 2026-03-25, although Fivetran, which now also owns dbt, remains the main influence.

'GX Cloud is the managed Great Expectations option' is out of date. FICO acquired it and it stopped being publicly available on 2026-06-01. GX Core is now stewarded by Fivetran at github.com/fivetran/great_expectations.
'Soda Core is Apache-2.0' is wrong for v4. Soda Core has been under ELv2 since January 2026, and PyPI lists it as 'Proprietary'.
'lakeFS is Apache-2.0' is wrong from v1.87.0 (2026-09-22), which is BSL 1.1 and forbids running a modified lakeFS in production. DVC is now stewarded by lakeFS (Nov 2025) and stays Apache-2.0.
'Vanna is the go-to open-source text-to-SQL library' is out of date. The GitHub repo is archived, and the last release was v2.0.2 (2026-02-02).
'WrenAI is AGPL' is out of date. In the current repo the core, sdk and skills are Apache-2.0, and AGPL is reserved only for possible future modules.
'Polars runs lazy queries in memory by default' is out of date. Polars 2.0 (2026-10-06) runs all lazy queries on the streaming, out-of-core engine and changes some SQL and Parquet semantics.
'DuckDB 1.4 is current' is out of date. Current is 1.5.6, DuckLake 1.0 has been stable since April 2026, and DuckDB 2.0 is in dev builds, expected fall 2026.
'FastMCP 2.x (jlowin/fastmcp)' is out of date. FastMCP is now PrefectHQ/fastmcp v4.1, on the MCP 2026-07-28 revision with sessionless requests and the Python SDK v2.
'PydanticAI 1.x' is out of date. 2.0 (2026-06-23) is a harness-first redesign built around 'capabilities'.
'Marquez is the maintained OpenLineage UI' is out of date. It has had no release since October 2024.
'MLflow is classical experiment tracking' is out of date. 3.x is a GenAI and agent ops server with tracing, LLM judges, an AI Gateway, an MCP Registry and RBAC.
design_implications: Add a license gate to the pipeline's supply-chain checks: an SBOM plus SPDX policy that flags ELv2, BSL, PLA, AGPL and 'Proprietary'. In 2025-2026 dbt Fusion, Soda Core and lakeFS were relicensed and MetricFlow was opened up. ELv2, BSL and PLA are fine for internal use but can block offering the pipeline as a hosted or managed service to customers, which matters if you sell this as SaaS.

(a) Recommended SMB / local-first minimal stack (all MIT or Apache): uv + Python 3.12/3.13; dlt for ingestion; DuckDB 1.5.x pinned, with DuckLake 1.0 or plain Parquet; Polars, pinned to 1.44.x until 2.0 semantics are tested; SQL transforms in dbt OSS v2, or dbt-core 1.12/1.13 for maximum stability, or SQLMesh; Pandera plus dbt tests for data contracts; Dagster OSS, or Prefect 3.8 for lighter flows; MLflow 3.x self-hosted for experiments, model registry, agent traces and evals; marimo for reproducible notebooks; agent layer on PydanticAI 2 or LangGraph 1.2; tools exposed through FastMCP 4; Inspect AI for offline agent evaluation; Cube Core or MetricFlow as the semantic layer that text-to-SQL agents must query through.

(b) Recommended enterprise stack with an existing warehouse: keep the warehouse (Snowflake, Databricks or BigQuery) as the system of record. Use Iceberg 1.12 tables behind an Iceberg REST catalog (vendor catalog or Unity Catalog OSS 0.7) for cross-engine access. Use dbt: the Fusion binary is acceptable for internal use, dbt OSS if you need zero proprietary terms. Use MetricFlow/OSI semantics and expose them to agents through dbt-mcp or Cube. Keep Airflow 3.3 if it is already there, otherwise use Dagster. Use GX Core or Pandera for quality checks and emit OpenLineage events into your existing catalog. Run MLflow 3.x with RBAC and the AI Gateway for agent governance and cost tracking, and LangGraph for long-running human-in-the-loop workflows.

Make agents reach data only through governed interfaces: semantic layer, MCP tools and read-only roles. Do not let them write raw SQL against production. Every 2026 vendor move (dbt Agents Schema, Wren and Cube MCP, the MLflow MCP Registry) points this way, and it is the main defense against wrong metrics.

Build the tool layer on MCP revision 2026-07-28 (FastMCP 4 / mcp SDK v2). Sessionless requests make horizontal scaling and gateway routing simple. Background tasks and interactive tools map directly onto long ETL or training jobs and onto approval steps.

Keep the agent orchestration code thin and swappable. PydanticAI (154 releases in 2026) and CrewAI (289) change fast. Pin exact versions and wrap them behind your own interfaces, so the durable state lives in your orchestrator and checkpoints, not in the framework.

Avoid or defer: Vanna (archived); smolagents and AutoGen for production (stalled); Marquez as a lineage backend (stale; consume OpenLineage events in your own store); Soda Core v4 and lakeFS 1.87+ if you might resell or host for customers or need to patch lakeFS; CrewAI for core paths (churn); Polars 2.0, DuckDB 2.0 and dbt v2 in production until you have run regression tests on your own data, because each has semantic or storage changes.

Reduce the risk of depending on one vendor. Fivetran now controls or heavily influences dbt, SQLMesh's origin, and GX Core stewardship. Anchor on open standards (SQL, Iceberg or DuckLake, OpenLineage, OSI semantics, MCP) so you could swap dbt for SQLMesh, or GX for Pandera, without rewriting the agent layer.

MLflow 3.x can replace several separate tools: experiment tracking, model registry, prompt registry, agent tracing, LLM judges and AI Gateway budgets. That is fewer services to run, which suits SMB deployments. Budget for its monthly releases and for coordinated database migrations, since 3.17 does not allow rolling upgrades.
open_questions: Can mainland-China environments reach the dbt platform for the Fusion binary's login-gated features? Should China deployments default to dbt OSS or SQLMesh to avoid a dependence on an external login?
Exact release date of DuckDB 2.0 and the Quack GA, and whether 2.0 changes the on-disk format or DuckLake catalog compatibility.

Long-term direction of GX Core under Fivetran stewardship (license, cadence, product overlap with dbt tests), and whether SQLMesh keeps its feature pace under the Linux Foundation now that releases have slowed since July 2026.
The full list of Polars 2.0 silent behavior changes. A third-party claim of 36 breaking changes and 75 removed APIs is not verified.
The exact date Vanna was archived (third parties say 2026-03-29) and whether a maintained community fork exists.
How Apache Ossie (incubating) relates formally to the Open Semantic Interchange specification, and whether Cube, Snowflake and other vendors implement it interoperably.

Corporate news for marimo, Evidently and Feast (funding, acquisitions, license plans) was not checked by search because the web-search budget ran out. Only their versions and repo activity were verified.
Whether the PLA terms for the dbt Fusion binary allow embedding it in a commercial agent product that runs inside customer environments, as opposed to a managed service. This needs legal review.

dimension: Economics, ROI and adoption reality of enterprise AI and agentic AI for data and analytics, 2025-2026

findings.claim: MIT NANDA's 'GenAI Divide' (2025) is a small, mostly self-reported study. Its '95%' means 95% of organizations report no measurable P&L impact from integrated or custom GenAI pilots. It does not mean 95% of AI projects fail. Generic chat tools convert well; custom enterprise tools mostly do not.
findings.evidence: Primary PDF text, research period Jan-Jun 2025. Method: review of 300+ public initiatives, interviews with 52 organizations, survey of 153 senior leaders recruited at 4 conferences. 'Successfully implemented' = users or executives remarked on a marked, sustained productivity and/or P&L impact. Funnel for enterprise-grade tools: 60% evaluated, 20% piloted, 5% reached production. Generic LLM chatbots: ~83% pilot-to-implementation. Vendor or partnership builds reached deployment ~67% of the time vs ~33% for internal builds. Mid-market top performers took ~90 days from pilot to full rollout; enterprises (>$100M revenue) took 9+ months. 40% of companies bought an LLM subscription, but employees at 90%+ of companies use personal AI tools.

findings.claim: Critiques of the MIT report are valid. The sample is small and drawn from conferences, success is self-defined, and the report contradicts itself on budgets. Larger surveys find mostly positive self-reported ROI. The direction of the finding (pilots stall) is supported; the exact number is not.
findings.evidence: The report itself says percentages 'reflect our interview sample of 52 organizations' and that success definitions varied. It puts sales and marketing at 50% of GenAI budgets in one place and ~70% (from a hypothetical $100 allocation exercise) in another. By contrast, Wharton/GBK 2025 (800+ leaders at US firms with >1,000 staff, published Oct 28 2025) found 3 in 4 report positive returns.

findings.claim: In the MIT data, the clearest ROI came from replacing external spend in back-office work (BPO contracts, agencies, outsourced risk checks), not from cutting internal staff.
findings.evidence: Back-office wins: BPO elimination worth $2-10M a year in customer service and document processing; 30% cut in external creative and content costs; $1M a year saved on outsourced risk checks in financial services. Front-office wins: lead qualification 40% faster, retention up 10%. The report says these gains came without material workforce reduction.

findings.claim: McKinsey State of AI 2026 ('On the road to ROI', Aug 25 2026): adoption and agent scaling grew, but EBIT impact did not move.
findings.evidence: 1,719 respondents, fielded May-June 2026. 37% attribute any EBIT impact to AI, 'about the same' as 2025. High performers (5%+ of EBIT from AI, impact called 'significant') flat at ~6%. At firms with $1B+ revenue, 40% scale agents (27% in 2025); at smaller firms, 22%. Nearly a third built software in-house with agentic coding tools instead of buying. 20% say AI operating costs limit use. 80% report better individual productivity. 39% expect AI job cuts next year (32% in 2025).

findings.claim: McKinsey State of AI 2025 (Nov 2025) baseline: AI use is near-universal, but agent scaling was limited and EBIT impact was mostly small.
findings.evidence: 88% use AI in at least one function. 62% experimenting with agents. 23% scaling agents somewhere, and no more than 10% in any single function. 39% report any EBIT impact, most of them under 5% of EBIT. About one-third have begun scaling AI. Figures come from secondary summaries because the primary page timed out.

findings.claim: Gartner (June 25 2025): more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end-2027. Most 'agentic' vendors are agent-washing: only ~130 of thousands are real.
findings.evidence: Stated causes: escalating costs, unclear business value, inadequate risk controls. Agent-washing means rebranding assistants, RPA and chatbots as agents. Jan 2025 Gartner poll (n=3,412): 19% made significant agentic investments, 42% conservative ones. Gartner advises redesigning workflows rather than bolting agents onto legacy systems. Gartner's Hype Cycle page: only 17% of organizations have deployed agents.

findings.claim: Gartner's 2026 warnings point to lock-in, layoffs-without-ROI and governance failure as the next problems.
findings.evidence: Sep 29 2026: 70% of enterprises will abandon agentic AI built by vendor forward-deployed engineers (FDE) by 2028. Through 2028, fewer than 20% of FDE engagements get turned into vendor product. Gartner also flags 'FDE washing'. May 5 2026 (350 executives): ~80% of organizations piloting autonomous capabilities cut staff without a matching ROI gain; agent software spend forecast at $206.5B for 2026. Mar 11 2026 D&A predictions: by 2030, half of agent deployment failures will come from weak runtime governance enforcement; analytic workflows should include a required evaluation stage. May 26 2026: uniform governance across all agents will cause agent failure.

findings.claim: Wharton/GBK 2026 (4th edition, Oct 13 2026): strong ROI is linked to tracking growth metrics. Approve-every-action oversight is linked to lower success. Token and API cost is now a top barrier.
findings.evidence: 1,416 respondents at US firms (1,000+ staff, >$50M revenue), fielded July 9-29 2026. 80% report positive returns; 28% strongly positive. Departments tracking a growth metric: 35% strong ROI vs 13% for efficiency-only. Most common metric is hours saved (40%); least common is net-new revenue (27%). Departments using agents to the fullest: 31% transformational success; approving every action: 16%. 64% call rising token, licence and API costs a major barrier. Only 40% are very confident they can track total AI spend. Correlational and self-reported; from a single secondary write-up.

findings.claim: BCG (Sept 2025, 'widening AI value gap'): value is concentrated in a few firms. Agentic AI is a growing share of the value those firms capture.
findings.evidence: 5% of firms are 'future-built'; 35% are scaling AI; 60% report hardly any material revenue or cost gains. Future-built firms get 5x the revenue increases and 3x the cost reductions of others. Agentic AI is ~17% of total AI value in 2025, expected 29% by 2028. Future-built firms put 15% of AI budgets into agents.

findings.claim: Deloitte State of AI in the Enterprise (2026 edition, survey Aug-Sep 2025): achieved benefits are mostly efficiency. Revenue growth is mostly aspirational, and agent governance is immature.
findings.evidence: 3,235 leaders in 24 countries. Achieved: productivity 66%, insights 53%, lower costs 40%, higher revenue 20%; 74% hope to grow revenue through AI. Only 1 in 5 has a mature governance model for autonomous agents. Insufficient worker skills is the biggest barrier.

findings.claim: Stanford AI Index 2026 (Apr 13 2026): adoption is broad, agent deployment is still single-digit in most functions, and agents fail roughly 1 in 3 times. Productivity gains are real but task-dependent.
findings.evidence: 88% organizational adoption (55% in 2023). Agent deployment in single digits across nearly all functions. OSWorld rose from ~12% to ~66% (human baseline 72.35%). Measured gains: customer support 14-15%, software development 26%, marketing output 50%; smaller on deep-reasoning tasks. Employment of software developers aged 22-25 fell nearly 20% from 2024. Top US vs top Chinese model gap on Arena: 2.7% (1,503 vs 1,464). Corporate AI investment: $581.69B in 2025.

findings.claim: The BCG/Harvard 'jagged frontier' RCT, now peer-reviewed: large gains on tasks inside the AI frontier, and large accuracy losses from over-trust on tasks outside it.
findings.evidence: 758 BCG consultants; published in Organization Science, March 2026. Inside the frontier: 12.2% more subtasks, ~25% faster, quality ~32% higher per the HBS page (the 2023 working paper reported >40%). Outside the frontier, correctness fell from 84.5% (no AI) to 70.6% (GPT-4) and 60% (GPT-4 plus prompt training).

findings.claim: Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond, QJE 2025 (customer support): +15% issues resolved per hour on average. Gains are concentrated among novices; top performers see small quality declines.
findings.evidence: 5,172 agents. The published figure is 15%; the 2023 working paper said 14% average and 34-35% for novices. Less experienced workers improve both speed and quality.

findings.claim: METR's developer RCT: the early-2025 '19% slower' result has been superseded. The late-2025 rerun points to a speedup, but METR calls the data unreliable because of selection bias.
findings.evidence: Original study: 16 developers, 246 tasks, +19% time (95% CI +2% to +39%), while developers believed they were ~20% faster. Feb 24 2026 update: 10 returning developers -18% (CI -38% to +9%); 47 new developers -4% (CI -15% to +9%). 30-50% of developers withheld tasks they would not do without AI. Pay fell from $150/hr to $50/hr. METR believes the true speedup is higher.

findings.claim: Agent task horizons keep growing fast, but they are measured at 50% reliability with wide error bars.
findings.evidence: METR: the 50% time horizon doubled about every 7 months over 2019-2025. Time Horizon 1.1 data: Claude Mythos Preview ~17.4h (CI 8.5-55h), Claude Opus 4.6 ~12h, Gemini 3.1 Pro ~6.4h, GPT-5.4 ~5.7h. METR says measurements above 16h are unreliable, and the page has not been updated since Sep 8 2026.

findings.claim: Official Western API list prices (USD per 1M tokens, Oct 2026): frontier-mid tiers sit around $2/$10. Small models are around $0.10/$0.50. Top 'astra/Fable' tiers are $10/$50.
findings.evidence: OpenAI: gpt-6.1-sol $2/$10 (cached input $0.10); gpt-6-astra $10/$50; gpt-5.5 $5/$30; gpt-6-luna $0.10/$0.50. Anthropic: Opus 5.5 $4/$20; Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10; Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50 for prompts up to 100K; Fable 5.1 $10/$50. Cache hits on Opus/Sonnet 5.5 cost 0.05x base input. For comparison, Opus 4/4.1 were $15/$75. Anthropic's tokenizer for Claude 4.7+ produces ~30% more tokens for the same text.

findings.claim: Chinese model API prices (Oct 2026) are still lower per token. However, the top Chinese tiers now approach Western mid-tier prices, and DeepSeek has peak-hour pricing.
findings.evidence: DeepSeek (official page): deepseek-flash (V4.1-Flash-1017) $0.15 in / $0.60 out off-peak, $0.30/$1.20 peak, cache hit $0.003-0.006. V4-Pro-0813: $0.66/$1.98 off-peak, $1.32/$3.96 peak. Peak hours: 01-04 and 06-10 UTC on weekdays. Z.ai: GLM-5.3 $1.4/$4.4; GLM-5.3-Flash $0.15/$0.50; GLM-4.7-Flash free. Kimi: K3 ¥20 in / ¥100 out (cache hit ¥2); K2.6 ¥6.5/¥27. Qwen official page not verified; trackers list Qwen3.7-Max at ~$1.25/$3.75.

findings.claim: The 'token prices only fall' trend broke in 2026. Chinese providers and some clouds raised prices because of a compute shortage, and agent workloads multiply tokens per task.
findings.evidence: AI Index 2025: GPT-3.5-level inference cost fell >280x between Nov 2022 and Oct 2024. In 2026: Zhipu raised its coding plan 30% (Feb) and prices 8-17% with GLM-5.1 (Apr). Alibaba Cloud compute rose 5-34%, Baidu 5-30%, Tencent ~5% (Apr-May). AWS EC2 for training +15% (Jan). DeepSeek raised V4 prices 50%-1,100% depending on meter, effective Aug 17, then partly cut Flash in Sep. Caixin (Apr 2026): firms rationing compute; DeepSeek had a ~12h outage; Zhipu's CEO says agent tools use tens to hundreds of times more tokens per task.

findings.claim: US data scientist cost: median wage $120,230. Fully loaded, roughly $170k+ before overhead.
findings.evidence: BLS: median $120,230 (May 2025 data); ~275,600 jobs; projected +35% growth 2025-2035. BLS ECEC (June 2026): wages are 70.0% and benefits 30.0% of private-industry compensation, so $120,230 / 0.70 ≈ $172k. Adding equipment, management and facilities overhead plausibly gives ~$190-220k; this is my derivation, not a BLS figure.

findings.claim: China analyst and engineer labor costs are roughly 1/3 to 1/2 of US levels in official averages. AI ROI built on replacing labor is therefore much weaker in China than in the US.
findings.evidence: NBS, 2025 average annual wages: IT sector ¥248,752 (non-private units) and ¥128,166 (private units); finance ¥211,164 (non-private); professional/technical staff in above-scale enterprises ¥155,491, with the IT-sector figure at ¥275,504. Tier-1 internet and finance data-scientist pay (often quoted at ¥300k-700k+) and employer social insurance plus housing fund (~30-40% on top) were not verified in this pass.

findings.claim: Evidence on self-serve analytics: production text-to-SQL saves real analyst time, but only with scoped domains, human confirmation and golden-set evaluation. Benchmark scores on SQL are near ceiling, while data-transformation tasks lag.
findings.evidence: Uber QueryGPT (Sep 2024): 1.2M interactive queries a month; authoring ~10 min vs ~3 min with QueryGPT; ~300 daily active users; 78% said it cut time. It needed domain workspaces, intent, table and column-prune agents, users confirming tables, and a golden-set evaluation. Hallucinated tables and columns remain unsolved. Spider 2.0 at launch: o1-preview 17.1%, GPT-4o 10.1%. Current leaderboard: Snow 96.70 (Genloop agent), Lite 76.23 (Tencent Tianqiong + GLM 5.2), DBT 65.6.

findings.claim: Headcount-reduction stories have been unreliable as an ROI basis.
findings.evidence: Klarna's own claims (Feb 27 2024): its AI assistant handled 2/3 of chats, did the work of 700 FTEs, cut resolution time from 11 to <2 minutes, and was worth an estimated $40M profit improvement in 2024. Gartner (June 10 2025): 50% of organizations will abandon plans to cut customer-service staff because of AI. Gartner (May 2026): layoffs create budget room but do not deliver returns. MIT: back-office gains came without material workforce reduction.

findings.claim: China policy pushes agent adoption hard. State Council 'AI+' Opinions (国发〔2025〕11号, Aug 21 2025) set agent and smart-terminal penetration targets above 70% by 2027 and above 90% by 2030. It also promotes datasets, annotation, synthetic data and agents-as-a-service.
findings.evidence: The text sets 2027 and 2030 penetration goals for 新一代智能终端 and 智能体 (new-generation smart terminals and agents). It promotes 智能原生企业 (AI-native enterprises), 智能体即服务 (agents-as-a-service), high-quality datasets, data annotation and synthetic data.

corrections_to_common_beliefs: 'MIT says 95% of AI projects fail' is wrong. The finding is that 95% of organizations in a small conference-based sample (52 organizations interviewed, 153 leaders surveyed) self-report no measurable P&L impact from integrated or custom pilots. Generic chat tools convert ~83% of pilots to implementation, and the report contradicts itself on budget shares (50% vs ~70%).

'Token prices only go down' is outdated for 2026. Western frontier per-token prices did fall (Opus $15/$75 down to Opus 5.5 at $4/$20; Sonnet tier to $2/$10). But Chinese providers and clouds raised prices amid a compute shortage: DeepSeek +50% to +1,100% in August 2026 plus peak pricing, Zhipu +30% then +8-17%, Alibaba, Baidu and Tencent compute +5-34%. Agent workloads also use tens to hundreds of times more tokens per task, so cost per task can rise even as price per token falls.

'Chinese models are nearly free' is no longer true at the top tier. Kimi K3 is ¥20 in / ¥100 out per 1M tokens (roughly $2.8/$14) and GLM-5.3 is $1.4/$4.4. Only Flash-class models (DeepSeek flash, GLM-5.3-Flash, GLM-4.7-Flash, which is free) stay near zero.

'METR proved AI makes developers 19% slower' is superseded. METR's Feb 2026 update shows point estimates of a speedup (-18% and -4% time) with wide intervals. METR says the data is unreliable because developers now refuse to work without AI.
Brynjolfsson's '14% average, 34% for novices' comes from the 2023 working paper. The published QJE 2025 version reports +15% on 5,172 agents.

The jagged-frontier quality gain of '>40%' is from the 2023 working paper. HBS describes the published Organization Science 2026 version as ~32% higher quality. The outside-frontier accuracy drop (84.5% to 60-70.6%) is the more important design lesson.

'Agents are now mainstream in the enterprise' overstates it. McKinsey 2026: 40% of $1B+ firms scale agents in at least one function, but only 22% of smaller firms. Stanford AI Index 2026: deployment is in single digits in nearly every function. EBIT impact is flat at 37%, and high performers at ~6%.

'Buy beats build' (MIT: ~67% vs ~33%) needs a caveat. McKinsey 2026 says nearly a third now build in-house with agentic coding tools instead of buying. Gartner predicts 70% will abandon agentic systems built by vendor forward-deployed engineers by 2028 because of cost and dependence. The lesson is to buy platforms but own the domain capability.

'Text-to-SQL only solves ~17% of enterprise tasks' (Spider 2.0 at launch, Nov 2024) is outdated. Top Spider 2.0-Snow scores are ~96.7 and Lite ~76. But data-transformation work (DBT, 65.6) and real enterprise schemas remain much harder, and benchmark scores do not equal production accuracy.
design_implications: Value model, cost side, in order of reliability: (1) Replace external spend: outsourced data operations and labeling, BPO reporting, consultants, ad-hoc agency analytics. MIT documents $2-10M a year in BPO savings and 30% lower agency costs. (2) Raise analyst and engineer throughput on tasks inside the frontier: SQL authoring went from ~10 to ~3 minutes at Uber, and pipeline code, docs and tests gain similarly. (3) Do not underwrite ROI on headcount cuts. Gartner, MIT and the Klarna history all show this is unreliable.

Value model, revenue side: use agents as a 'factory' that builds, monitors and retrains classic predictive models (demand forecasting, pricing, churn uplift, fraud and risk scoring, marketing mix). The value of those models is proven by holdout or A/B tests. Wharton 2026: departments tracking growth metrics report strong ROI 35% of the time vs 13% for efficiency-only. Every pipeline output should carry a business KPI hook, not just hours saved.

China vs global: Chinese IT wages average ¥128k-¥249k (NBS 2025) vs a ~$170k+ fully loaded US data scientist. Labor substitution alone rarely pays back in China. Make the China business case on speed to decision, scale (more models, SKUs or regions per analyst), revenue KPIs, and 'AI+' policy-driven demand (70% agent penetration target by 2027). Default to domestic models (DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, Kimi) for compliance and cost.

Unit economics: budget per task, not per token. Build in: model routing (cheap tier at ~$0.10-0.30 input — Haiku 5.5, gpt-6-luna, deepseek-flash, GLM-5.3-Flash — for extraction, classification and SQL drafts; frontier tier at $2-10 input only for planning and hard reasoning); prompt-cache-heavy design (cache hits cost 0.05-0.1x); batch and off-peak scheduling (DeepSeek off-peak is 50% off; OpenAI batch 50%); token and cost budgets per run; spend telemetry (only 40% of firms are confident they can track AI spend). Account for Claude 4.7+ tokenizer inflation (~30%).

Plan for supply and price risk: keep a provider-agnostic model gateway with at least 2-3 vendors (including one domestic and one self-hostable open-weights model), fallbacks, and a re-pricing alarm. 2026 brought DeepSeek price hikes and peak pricing, Zhipu and cloud hikes, Chinese compute rationing and a ~12h DeepSeek outage.

Evaluation first: before any agent ships, build golden question and answer sets from real logs, plus decoupled component evaluations (intent, table selection, SQL validity, result correctness), as Uber did. Make the evaluation stage a mandatory pipeline step, as Gartner's 2026 D&A guidance recommends. Treat public benchmarks (Spider 2.0, OSWorld) only as capability signals.

Data readiness is the gating investment: a semantic layer or curated domain 'workspaces', metadata and lineage, data contracts, and access control. Build this before agents. Hallucinated tables and columns remain unsolved without it.

Calibrate autonomy by risk tier instead of making humans approve every step. Wharton links approve-every-action setups to 16% transformational success vs 31% for full use. Gartner warns uniform governance across agents causes failure. Use auto-execution for reversible, low-risk steps; human gates for writes to production data, model promotion and customer-facing decisions; and sampled audits.

Keep humans on out-of-frontier tasks: novel causal claims, ambiguous business judgement, anything without ground truth. The BCG RCT shows over-trust cut correctness from 84.5% to 60-70.6%. Require agents to emit evidence such as queries, data snapshots and test results so humans can verify cheaply.

Build vs buy: buy commodity layers (LLM APIs, warehouse-native NL2SQL, orchestration, observability). Build and own the domain layer: semantic models, golden sets, evaluation harness, playbooks, business-metric linkage. If using vendor forward-deployed engineers, contract for IP ownership, knowledge transfer and an exit plan from day one (Gartner predicts 70% FDE abandonment by 2028).

Scope pilots to about 90 days with a pre-agreed P&L or KPI baseline and a kill criterion. Mid-market winners reach production in ~90 days, while enterprises take 9+ months and convert least. Target ignored back-office and analytics-operations workflows first, where payback is clearest.

Avoid: agent-washed products (Gartner: ~130 genuine vendors among thousands); 'chatbot over the warehouse' with no semantic layer or evaluations; ROI decks built on hours saved alone; single-vendor lock-in; agents doing long autonomous work beyond their reliable horizon without checkpoints (METR horizons are measured at 50% success).
